title: 水能记住旧情，氢弹重新定义和平
subtitle: 1991年首届盛典：当《自然》水记忆奇文、诺奖精子库与垃圾债券之父同台加冕

article_paragraphs: 1991年金秋，科学幽默杂志《不可思议研究年刊》主编马克·亚伯拉罕斯在麻省理工学院博物馆点燃了第一把荒诞与理性交织的火炬——首届搞笑诺贝尔奖正式横空出世。在这场笑声震天动地的开山盛典上，组委会不仅颁出了七项载入史册的真实大奖，还在元年附赠了三项后来被官方坦承为虚构彩蛋并永久剔除出正统名录的戏仿奖项，由此一举奠定了“初看让人捧腹发笑，细想引人掩卷深思”的评奖圭臬。

在自然科学阵营里，法国免疫学家雅克·本维尼斯特凭一篇震碎《自然》杂志编辑部三观的奇文高票摘得化学奖：他执着地宣称普通的水竟是一种“高智商液体”，哪怕把抗体溶液反复稀释到连半个溶质分子都不复存在，纯水依然拥有刻骨铭心的“水记忆力”，能够记住昔日溶质留下的深情往事。生物学奖颁给了优生学狂热分子罗伯特·克拉克·格雷厄姆，这位自诩的繁衍先知创办了大名鼎鼎的“生殖选择库”，傲慢地规定只接收诺贝尔奖得主与奥运冠军的精子捐赠，妄图用冷冻试管批量孵化人类天才精英。相比之下，医学奖得主艾伦·克利格曼则堪称造福苍生的餐桌活菩萨，他潜心研发的防胀气滴剂“豆乐”能够精准分解豆类多糖，彻底消灭了消化道浊气，将亿万食客从社交场合响屁连天、腹胀如鼓的尴尬深渊中解救出来。

社会与人文领域的四大奖项更是把辛辣讽刺拉到了满格。经济学奖颁给了华尔街呼风唤雨的“垃圾债券之父”迈克尔·米尔肯，致敬这位凭高风险金融魔术让全世界都欠他一笔巨债的资本大鳄；文学奖授予畅销奇书《众神之车》作者埃里希·冯·丹尼肯，感谢这位故事大王脑洞大开地将金字塔等古代文明奇迹统统归功于远古外星宇航员的降临指点。时任美国副总统丹·奎尔因屡次闹出拼写与科学常识笑话，被评委会册封为“消耗时间与占据空间的人”并获颁教育奖，因为他用自身言行比任何人都更雄辩地证明了普及科学教育是何等迫在眉睫；而首届和平奖则颁给了“氢弹之父”兼“星球大战”天基武器系统头号推手爱德华·泰勒——毕竟纵观二十世纪，实在没人比他更卖力地用核威慑重新定义了人类对“和平”二字的理解。

prizes.winners: 雅克·本维尼斯特 (Jacques Benveniste)
prizes.summary: 执着证明水（H₂O）是一种“聪明液体”，在溶质痕迹完全消失后仍能保留对过往事件的“水记忆”。
prizes.winners_en: Jacques Benveniste
prizes.summary_en: For his persistent discovery that water (H₂O) is an intelligent liquid capable of remembering events long after all trace of those events has vanished.

title_en: Water With a Memory and H-Bombs Redefining Peace
subtitle_en: The 1991 Inaugural Ceremony: Where Sentient H₂O, a Nobel Sperm Bank, and the Junk Bond King Took the Stage
article_paragraphs_en: In the autumn of 1991, science humor editor Marc Abrahams and his colleagues gathered at the MIT Museum in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to light a torch of rational absurdity: the inaugural Ig Nobel Prize ceremony had arrived. Conceived to celebrate unusual achievements that 'first make people laugh, and then make them think,' that historic opening night presented seven genuine awards—alongside three tongue-in-cheek prizes for apocryphal achievements that were later officially retired from the canonical archive. Together, they set the gold standard for honoring human endeavours where high ambition collides head-on with unintended comedy, launching a beloved annual academic tradition supported by genuine Nobel laureates that would soon captivate scientists, students, and skeptics around the globe.

Leading the natural sciences, French immunologist Jacques Benveniste—prolific proselytizer and dedicated correspondent of the prestigious journal Nature—captured the Chemistry Prize for his persistent discovery that ordinary water (H₂O) is in fact an 'intelligent liquid.' Through extreme serial dilutions, Benveniste demonstrated to his own complete satisfaction that water is able to remember biological events long after every last trace of the original dissolved antibody molecules has vanished from the test tube. In Biology, selector of seeds and prophet of propagation Robert Klark Graham was honored for his pioneering development of the Repository for Germinal Choice, an elite California sperm bank designed to breed super-geniuses by accepting genetic donations exclusively from Nobel laureates and Olympic champions. Bringing laboratory science back down to the dinner table, Alan Kligerman—celebrated as the deviser of digestive deliverance and vanquisher of vapor—won the Medicine Prize for inventing Beano, the pioneering enzymatic liquid that breaks down complex sugars to prevent bloat, gassiness, gastrointestinal discomfort, and acute social embarrassment after eating beans and legumes.

The social, political, and literary prizes delivered equally razor-sharp satire. Wall Street titan Michael Milken, revered and reviled as the father of the high-yield 'junk bond,' was awarded the Economics Prize as a financial wizard 'to whom the entire world is indebted' while serving time for securities violations. Visionary Swiss raconteur Erich von Däniken claimed the Literature Prize for his best-selling book Chariots of the Gods?, which breathlessly explained how ancient human civilization, pyramids, and monolithic monuments were shaped by visiting astronauts from outer space. In Education, then-U.S. Vice President J. Danforth Quayle—officially cited as a 'consumer of time and occupier of space'—was honored for demonstrating, better than anyone else in public life, the urgent need for science education through his unforgettable public gaffes. Finally, the first-ever Ig Nobel Peace Prize saluted physicist Edward Teller, father of the thermonuclear hydrogen bomb and chief champion of the 'Star Wars' Strategic Defense Initiative weapons system, for his lifelong efforts to permanently change the meaning of peace as we know it through thermonuclear deterrence.

article_paragraphs: 1992年的第二届搞笑诺贝尔奖将聚光灯投向了实验室与日常生活交汇处的荒诞火花。日本横滨资生堂研究中心的神田不二宏、八木荣一郎、福田实、中岛敬介、太田忠男与中田兴亚六位学者勇夺医学奖，他们在《英国皮肤病学杂志》发表了硬核论文《脚臭化学成分的阐明》，动用精密仪器分析鞋袜里的低级脂肪酸后，得出了一个震古烁今的哲学结论：凡是觉得自己有脚臭的人确实有脚臭，觉得自己没有的人就真的没有！化学奖颁给了胶体化学家伊薇特·巴萨，表彰她合成出令小朋友欢呼雀跃的“亮蓝色果冻”，堪称二十世纪人工色素与胶体化学的巅峰结晶；而营养学奖则致敬了斯帕姆午餐肉的广大食客，感谢他们五十四年来不挑食的顽强消化能力。

有些得主靠脑洞封神，有些得主则凭“好心办坏事”与离谱造假载入史册。法国新教童子军组织“法国探路者”本想做件公益好事去清理岩洞里的现代涂鸦，结果少年们干劲太足，操起钢丝刷把布鲁尼凯勒附近梅里耶尔洞穴岩壁上拥有上万年历史的史前远古野牛壁画给刷得干干净净，含泪捧走考古学奖。英国的道格·鲍尔与大卫·乔利两位老汉则摘得物理学奖，他俩承认多年来趁夜潜入麦田用木板和绳子压出几何图案，以“麦田怪圈”为低能物理学界的“场论”做出了字面意义上的画圈贡献。更离谱的是生物学奖得主塞西尔·雅各布森医生，这位生殖诊所专家发明了“单手操作”的精子库质量控制法——偷偷用自己的精子让数十位不知情的女患者受孕，成了名副其实的“造人族长”。

学术圈与公共领域的奇观同样精彩绝伦。莫斯科元素有机化合物研究所的尤里·斯特鲁奇科夫在十年间署名发表了惊人的九百四十八篇科学论文，平均每三点九天就产出一篇，凭一己之力将学术灌水推向极致而斩获文学奖。艺术奖由吉姆·诺尔顿与美国国家艺术基金会共享，前者绘制了经典解剖海报《动物王国的阴茎》，后者竟慷慨拨款资助他将其改造成一本立体翻翻书。经济学奖颁给了拒绝为巨额亏损买单、试图“为灾难本身投保”的伦敦劳合社投资者；和平奖则授予前洛杉矶警察局长达里尔·盖茨，嘲讽他用引发全城大暴动的独特执法手腕，“极具说服力地把各族民众团结在了一起”。

title_en: If You Think Your Feet Stink, Science Says They Do
subtitle_en: The 1992 Ceremony: From Shiseido's Foot-Odor Sleuths and Cave-Scrubbing Scouts to a Paper Every 3.9 Days
article_paragraphs_en: The second Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1992 turned the spotlight on the delightful intersection of meticulous laboratory instrumentation and everyday human folly. Six researchers at the Shiseido Research Center in Yokohama—F. Kanda, E. Yagi, M. Fukuda, K. Nakajima, T. Ohta, and O. Nakata—captured the Medicine Prize for their landmark paper in the British Journal of Dermatology, 'Elucidation of Chemical Compounds Responsible for Foot Malodour.' After analyzing short-chain fatty acids and isovaleric acid from sweaty socks, the team arrived at an immortal philosophical truth: people who think they have foot odor actually do, and those who think they don't, don't. In Chemistry, constructor of colorful colloids Ivette Bassa was celebrated for her decisive role in the crowning achievement of twentieth-century food chemistry: the synthesis of bright blue Jell-O. Meanwhile, the Nutrition Prize saluted the courageous consumers of Spam—utilizers of canned comestibles—for fifty-four years of undiscriminating digestion.

While some laureates triumphed through curiosity, others achieved lasting fame through overzealous blunders or audacious misconduct. The Archaeology Prize was awarded to Éclaireurs de France, a fresh-scrubbed French Protestant youth group whose name translates to 'those who show the way.' Embarking on a well-intentioned mission to scrub modern graffiti off the walls of the Meyrières Cave near the village of Bruniquel, the energetic scouts inadvertently scoured away priceless prehistoric cave paintings of bison dating back more than ten thousand years. In Physics, Englishmen David Chorley and Doug Bower—hailed as lions of low-energy physics—won for their circular contributions to 'field theory' based on the geometrical destruction of English crops, confessing how they had flattened wheat fields at night with planks and ropes to create Britain's famous crop circles. Even more brazen was Biology laureate Dr. Cecil Jacobson, a relentlessly generous fertility specialist who devised a 'simple, single-handed method of quality control' by secretly using his own sperm to impregnate dozens of unsuspecting patients.

Academic hyper-productivity, anatomical art, and institutional hubris completed the 1992 roster. Moscow crystallographer Yuri Struchkov of the Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds won the Literature Prize as an unstoppable author credited with publishing 948 scientific papers between 1981 and 1990—averaging more than one peer-reviewed paper every 3.9 days. The Art Prize went jointly to modern Renaissance man Jim Knowlton for his classic comparative anatomy poster 'Penises of the Animal Kingdom,' and to the U.S. National Endowment for the Arts for encouraging him to extend his work in the form of a pop-up book. Finally, the Economics Prize cited the investors of Lloyd's of London—heirs to 300 years of dull, prudent management—for their bold attempt to insure disaster by refusing to pay for their company's catastrophic losses, while former Los Angeles Police Chief Daryl Gates received the Peace Prize for his 'uniquely compelling methods of bringing people together.'

article_paragraphs: 1993年的第三届搞笑诺贝尔奖一口气颁出十一项大奖，堪称奇葩学术研究的满汉全席。生物学奖得主保罗·威廉姆斯与肯尼思·纽厄尔化身为追踪猪粪的生物侦探，发表了妙趣横生的《兜风生猪的沙门氏菌排泄情况》，严肃论证生猪坐车兜风时的旅途颠簸与紧张兴奋如何显著促进沙门氏菌排泄。医学奖则让天下男士闻之双腿一紧：詹姆斯·诺兰、托马斯·斯蒂尔韦尔与约翰·桑兹三位急诊科好人凭借《拉链卡住阴茎的急性处理》获奖，为这一火烧眉毛的男科惨剧提供了用骨剪剪断拉链滑块横梁的无痛解救方案。而文学奖则颁给了埃里克·托波尔等四位领衔学者及其多达九百七十二名共同作者——他们在《新英格兰医学杂志》发表了一篇仅十页的心肌梗死溶栓论文，作者人数竟是页数的整整一百倍！

在科学与伪科学的跨界地带，各路奇人异士更是大显神通。哈佛医学院的约翰·麦克与天普大学的大卫·雅各布斯共享心理学奖，他们经过深度访谈后跳跃性地断言：那些相信自己被外星人绑架的人八成真被绑架过，而且“外星人绑架地球人的核心目的是为了繁衍后代”。法国学者路易·凯尔夫兰凭一腔炼金术热情摘得物理学奖，他信誓旦旦地宣称母鸡能在体内通过“生物冷聚变”过程，把吃进去的钾和硅凭空转化为鸡蛋壳里的钙质。南卡罗来纳州的罗伯特·费德则将统计学用到了神学极致，他精确算出苏联前领导人戈尔巴乔夫是“敌基督”的概率高达七十一亿亿分之一，一举斩获数学奖。

商业与技术发明同样令人拍案叫绝。深夜电视购物大王罗恩·波佩尔凭切菜神器、口袋钓鱼竿、麦克风先生以及“蛋壳内搅蛋器”重新定义了工业革命，荣膺消费工程学奖；发明家杰伊·希夫曼因造出让司机边开车边看电视的投影设备，与居然投票立法批准该设备的密歇根州议会共享前瞻技术奖；田纳西州的坎贝尔兄弟则因发明夹在杂志书页间、熏得读者直打喷嚏的“香水试纸条”拿到化学奖。此外，经济学家拉维·巴特拉靠狂销畅销书《1990年大萧条》“凭一己之力阻止了全球经济崩溃”而获经济学奖；菲律宾百事可乐公司则因瓶盖抽奖报错中奖号码，瞬间激怒并团结了八十万名持盖民众，让原本敌对的各路派系首次同仇敌忾，荒诞摘得和平奖。

title_en: Joy-Riding Pigs, Zipper Emergencies, and 976 Authors on Ten Pages
subtitle_en: The 1993 Ceremony: Chicken Cold Fusion, Dashboard TVs, and the Exact Odds That Gorbachev Is the Antichrist
article_paragraphs_en: Expanding to eleven eclectic categories, the third Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1993 served up a grand banquet of unforgettable empirical inquiries. In Biology, bold biological detectives Paul Williams Jr. of the Oregon State Health Division and Kenneth W. Newell of the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine were honored for their pioneering public-health investigation, 'Salmonella Excretion in Joy-Riding Pigs,' which carefully tracked how taking swine out for a vehicular spin triggers bacterial shedding. The Medicine Prize made men everywhere wince in instant sympathy: medical men of mercy James F. Nolan, Thomas J. Stillwell, and John P. Sands Jr. won for their painstaking emergency-room report, 'Acute Management of the Zipper-Entrapped Penis,' detailing how to rescue patients by snipping the zipper's median bar. Meanwhile, the Literature Prize went to Eric Topol, R. Califf, F. Van de Werf, P. W. Armstrong, and their 972 co-authors from fifteen countries for publishing a ten-page cardiology paper in The New England Journal of Medicine that featured one hundred times as many authors as pages.

On the wild frontier between bold speculation, alchemy, and apocalyptic statistics, three prizes stood out. Harvard Medical School psychiatrist John Mack and Temple University historian David Jacobs shared the Psychology Prize as mental visionaries for their leaping conclusion that people who believe they were kidnapped by aliens from outer space probably were—and especially for their clinical deduction that 'the focus of the abduction is the production of children.' In Physics, French alchemical admirer Louis Kervran was cited for his conclusion that the calcium in chickens' eggshells is created inside the hen by a biological process of cold fusion. Not to be outdone in mathematical rigor, farsighted statistical seer Robert Faid of Greenville, South Carolina, captured the Mathematics Prize for calculating the exact odds—710,609,175,188,282,000 to 1—that former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev is the Antichrist.

Commercial ingenuity, legislative madness, and corporate blunders provided the final fireworks of 1993. Incessant inventor and late-night television pitchman Ron Popeil won the Consumer Engineering Prize for redefining the industrial revolution with devices such as the Veg-O-Matic, the Pocket Fisherman, Mr. Microphone, and the Inside-the-Shell Egg Scrambler. The Visionary Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Michigan inventor Jay Schiffman for creating AutoVision—a head-up projection device that makes it possible to drive a car and watch television at the same time—and to the Michigan state legislature for making it legal to do so. Brothers James and Gaines Campbell of Lookout Mountain, Tennessee, took Chemistry for inventing magazine perfume scent strips, while Southern Methodist University economist Ravi Batra won Economics for selling enough copies of his best-sellers The Great Depression of 1990 ($17.95) and Surviving the Great Depression of 1990 ($18.95) to single-handedly prevent worldwide economic collapse. Finally, Pepsi-Cola of the Philippines won the Peace Prize for announcing the wrong winning number in a millionaire contest, inciting and uniting 800,000 riotously expectant winners and bringing warring factions together for the first time in their nation's history.

article_paragraphs: 1994年的第四届搞笑诺贝尔奖堪称人类“硬核自残与迷之执着”的巅峰大赏（官方事后还严谨地剔除了一项源于失实媒体报道的乌龙奖项，保留九项真凭实据的传世杰作）。医学奖破天荒一分为二：前美国海军陆战队员“X患者”在被自家宠物响尾蛇咬伤嘴唇后，深信民间电击解毒偏方，执意让邻居把汽车火花塞电线夹在自己嘴唇上，将汽车引擎轰到每分钟三千转整整电击了五分钟；而理查德·达特与理查德·古斯塔夫森两位急诊专家则因将这一惨烈抢救写成论文《电击疗法治疗响尾蛇咬伤的失败》共同获奖。同样对自己下狠手的还有纽约兽医罗伯特·洛佩兹，他为了弄清猫耳螨会不会传染给人，亲自从猫耳朵里掏出耳螨塞进自己耳道，悉心体验并记录奇痒难耐的全过程，实至名归地捧走昆虫学奖。

军旅与政坛的入选者则展示了另类的数据控与管理术。布赖恩·斯威尼等四位美军军医凭《便秘的军人：驻外美军中的患病率》摘得生物学奖，他们深入战地对前线美军官兵的排便频率进行了极其详尽的统计学摸底。心理学奖颁给了新加坡前总理李光耀，表彰他长达三十年对三百万新加坡公民一旦吐痰、嚼口香糖或喂鸽子就予以重罚的“负强化心理学”大型社会实验。得克萨斯州参议员鲍勃·格拉斯哥则因在1989年推动一项奇葩禁毒法案荣膺化学奖——该法案规定公民未经官方许可购买烧杯、烧瓶或试管等实验室玻璃器皿统统违法，差点把全州中学化学老师送进警察局。

至于宗教、玄学与金融领域的跨界表现，更是让人啼笑皆非。玛赫西大学的物理学家约翰·哈格林宣称召集四千名受训冥想者集体发功，成功让华盛顿特区的暴力犯罪率下降了百分之十八，由此获颁和平奖；阿拉巴马州美南浸信会运用数学模型逐县估算全州有多少公民如果不悔改就会下地狱，摘得数学奖；山达基教创始人兼科幻作家罗恩·哈伯德则凭那本为自己赚得盆满钵满的畅销书《戴尼提》获追授文学奖。而经济学奖得主、智利国家铜业公司交易员胡安·巴勃罗·达维拉则上演了史诗级手滑：他在电脑上把“卖出”误敲成“买入”，随后为补窟窿疯狂加仓，最终亏掉智利国民生产总值的千分之五，还让智利人用他的名字造出了新动词“达维拉尔”（意为“把事情彻底搞砸”）。

prizes.winners: W·布赖恩·斯威尼 (W. Brian Sweeney) 等四人
prizes.summary: 发表突破性研究《便秘的军人：驻外美军中的患病率》，对官兵排便频率进行详尽数值分析。

prizes.summary_en: For their breakthrough study 'The Constipated Serviceman: Prevalence Among Deployed US Troops' and its numerical analysis of bowel movement frequency.

prizes.winners: 约翰·哈格林 (John Hagelin，玛赫西大学)
prizes.summary: 通过实验得出结论：4000名受训冥想者集体发功，使华盛顿特区的暴力犯罪率下降了18%。
prizes.winners_en: John Hagelin (Maharishi University)
prizes.summary_en: Promulgator of peaceful thoughts, for his experimental conclusion that 4,000 trained meditators caused an 18 percent decrease in violent crime in Washington, D.C.

prizes.winners: “X患者”与理查德·达特 (Richard C. Dart)、理查德·古斯塔夫森医生
prizes.summary: 前者被响尾蛇咬伤后用汽车火花塞夹住嘴唇以3000转引擎电击五分钟，后者撰写报告证实该电击疗法彻底失败。
prizes.winners_en: 'Patient X' and Drs. Richard C. Dart and Richard A. Gustafson
prizes.summary_en: For shocking a rattlesnake-bitten lip with car sparkplug wires at 3,000 rpm for five minutes, and for the report 'Failure of Electric Shock Treatment for Rattlesnake Envenomation.'

prizes.winners: 罗伯特·洛佩兹 (Robert A. Lopez)
prizes.summary: 把从猫耳朵里取出的耳螨塞进自己耳道里，亲自观察、记录并分析人感染猫耳螨的结果。
prizes.winners_en: Robert A. Lopez
prizes.summary_en: Valiant veterinarian, for obtaining ear mites from cats, inserting them into his own ear, and carefully observing and analyzing the results.

prizes.winners: 李光耀 (Lee Kuan Yew，新加坡前总理)
prizes.summary: 开展长达三十年的负强化心理学研究，对三百万新加坡公民每逢吐痰、嚼口香糖或喂鸽子即予以处罚。
prizes.winners_en: Lee Kuan Yew (Former Prime Minister of Singapore)
prizes.summary_en: Practitioner of negative reinforcement, for his thirty-year study of punishing three million citizens whenever they spat, chewed gum, or fed pigeons.

prizes.winners: L·罗恩·哈伯德 (L. Ron Hubbard)
prizes.summary: 科幻作家兼山达基教创始人，撰写出对人类（或其中一部分人）利润丰厚的畅销书《戴尼提》。
prizes.winners_en: L. Ron Hubbard
prizes.summary_en: Author of science fiction and founding father of Scientology, for his crackling book Dianetics, which is highly profitable to mankind or a portion thereof.

prizes.winners: 得克萨斯州参议员鲍勃·格拉斯哥 (Bob Glasgow)
prizes.summary: 发起1989年禁毒法，规定未经许可购买烧杯、烧瓶、试管等实验室玻璃器皿均属违法。
prizes.winners_en: Texas State Senator Bob Glasgow
prizes.summary_en: For sponsoring the 1989 drug control law making it illegal to purchase beakers, flasks, test tubes, or other laboratory glassware without a permit.

prizes.winners: 胡安·巴勃罗·达维拉 (Juan Pablo Dávila)
prizes.summary: 误把期货指令“卖出”输成“买入”，试图翻本却最终亏掉智利GNP的0.5%，催生新动词“davilar”（彻底搞砸）。
prizes.winners_en: Juan Pablo Dávila (Codelco, Chile)
prizes.summary_en: For instructing his computer to 'buy' when he meant 'sell' and losing 0.5% of Chile's GNP, inspiring the new verb 'davilar' ('to botch things up royally').

prizes.winners: 阿拉巴马州美南浸信会 (The Southern Baptist Church of Alabama)
prizes.summary: 运用数学方法逐县精确估算：如果阿拉巴马州公民不悔改，全州究竟有多少人会下地狱。
prizes.winners_en: The Southern Baptist Church of Alabama
prizes.summary_en: Mathematical measurers of morality, for their county-by-county estimate of how many Alabama citizens will go to Hell if they do not repent.

title_en: Sparkplugs on a Snakebitten Lip and Cat Ear Mites in a Vet's Own Ear
subtitle_en: The 1994 Ceremony: Self-Experimentation, Constipated Troops, and the Trader Who Botched 0.5% of Chile's GNP
article_paragraphs_en: The fourth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony in 1994 stood as a monument to heroic self-experimentation and stubborn human persistence—comprising nine verified prizes after one award based on erroneous press accounts was officially removed. The Medicine Prize was presented in two unforgettable parts: first to 'Patient X,' a valiant former U.S. Marine who, after suffering a venomous bite on the lip from his pet rattlesnake, insisted on attaching automobile sparkplug wires to his lip while the car engine was revved to 3,000 rpm for five minutes; and second to Drs. Richard C. Dart of the Rocky Mountain Poison Center and Richard A. Gustafson of the University of Arizona for their well-grounded clinical report, 'Failure of Electric Shock Treatment for Rattlesnake Envenomation.' Matching that personal sacrifice, veterinarian Robert A. Lopez of Westport, New York—friend of all creatures great and small—won the Entomology Prize for extracting ear mites from cats, inserting them into his own ear canal, and carefully observing and analyzing the resulting torment in 'Of Mites and Man.'

Military logistics, behavioral conditioning, and legislative logic also earned top honors in 1994. Four military physicians—W. Brian Sweeney, Brian Krafte-Jacobs, Jeffrey W. Britton, and Wayne Hansen—won the Biology Prize for their breakthrough study in Military Medicine, 'The Constipated Serviceman: Prevalence Among Deployed US Troops,' featuring an exhaustive numerical analysis of bowel-movement frequency on the front lines. In Psychology, former Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew of Singapore was recognized as a master practitioner of the psychology of negative reinforcement for his thirty-year empirical study of the effects of punishing three million citizens whenever they spat, chewed gum, or fed pigeons. Meanwhile, Texas State Senator Bob Glasgow captured the Chemistry Prize as a wise writer of logical legislation for sponsoring a 1989 drug-control law that made it illegal to purchase beakers, flasks, test tubes, or other laboratory glassware without a permit.

Spiritual statistics, profitable prose, and financial catastrophe completed the 1994 chronicle. Physicist John Hagelin of Maharishi University and the Institute of Science, Technology and Public Policy received the Peace Prize as a promulgator of peaceful thoughts for his experimental conclusion that 4,000 trained meditators caused an 18 percent decrease in violent crime in Washington, D.C. The Mathematics Prize went to the Southern Baptist Church of Alabama—mathematical measurers of morality—for their county-by-county estimate of how many Alabama citizens will go to Hell if they do not repent, while science-fiction author and Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard won Literature for his crackling Good Book Dianetics, which proved highly profitable to mankind or to a portion thereof. Finally, tireless Chilean futures trader Juan Pablo Dávila of the state-owned Codelco company won Economics for instructing his computer to 'buy' when he meant 'sell,' and subsequently attempting to recoup his losses with increasingly unprofitable trades that lost 0.5 percent of Chile's gross national product—inspiring his countrymen to coin the verb 'davilar,' meaning 'to botch things up royally.'

article_paragraphs: 1995年10月，第五届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院首次实现全球网络直播，十项大奖将学术界的猎奇求知欲展现得淋漓尽致。日本庆应义塾大学的渡边茂、坂本淳子与胁田真纯团队荣膺心理学奖，他们通过麻籽投喂奖励，成功训练鸽子精准分辨莫奈的印象派风景与毕加索的立体派画作，证明鸟类的艺术鉴赏力绝不含糊。英国诺里奇食品研究所的乔治特、帕克与史密斯三位学者则将力学武器对准早餐碗，发表《含水量对早餐麦片压实行为影响的研究》，因严谨分析脆麦片泡软塌陷的物理过程而摘得物理学奖；亚特兰大商人约翰·马丁内斯则因向世界推广由印尼椰子猫吞食咖啡果并排泄出的昂贵“猫屎咖啡”获颁营养学奖。

人体奥秘与日常微末小事同样逃不过科学家们的法眼。威斯康星州的医学专家大卫·布什与詹姆斯·斯塔林凭借《直肠异物：病例报告与世界文献综合评述》勇夺文学奖，这篇旷世综述宛如一部人类菊部收纳百科全书，记录了七个灯泡、磨刀器、两把电筒、塞着土豆的油壶、珠宝锯、冰冻猪尾巴，甚至还有一位患者体内同时藏着眼镜、行李箱钥匙、烟草袋和一本杂志的惊人“四件套”收藏！挪威与丹麦学者玛莎·巴克维格和露丝·尼尔森因深入研究《寒冷环境下湿内裤对体温调节反应及热舒适度的影响》获颁公共卫生奖；玛西亚·比贝尔、大卫·尚纳霍夫与迈克尔·博伊尔三人凭研究堵住单侧鼻孔呼吸如何影响大脑认知摘得医学奖；牙医罗伯特·博蒙特则靠调查《患者对打蜡与未打蜡牙线的偏好》拿下牙医学奖。

在商业、金融与政坛领域，讽刺火力更是全开。比佛利山庄的设计师比扬·帕克扎德推出了大名鼎鼎的“基因古龙水”与“基因香水”——妙就妙在这款香水里既不含一丁点脱氧核糖核酸，瓶身还被设计成了违背双螺旋常识的“三螺旋”造型，毫无悬念地拿下化学奖。经济学奖由搞垮百年巴林银行的魔鬼交易员尼克·里森及其上司，与令加州奥兰治县破产的罗伯特·西特龙共享，感谢他们用金融衍生品微积分证明了“任何金融机构都是有极限的”。而和平奖则颁给了台湾立法院，表彰议员们用拳打脚踢、飞身锁喉的议场全武行向世界证明：政客互殴比对外发动战争划算多了。

title_en: Art-Critic Pigeons, Soggy Cereal Physics, and Wet Underwear in the Cold
subtitle_en: The 1995 Ceremony: Civet-Excreted Coffee, an Encyclopedia of Rectal Foreign Bodies, and DNA-Free Triple-Helix Perfume
article_paragraphs_en: Broadcast live over the internet from Harvard's Sanders Theatre for the very first time on October 6, 1995, the fifth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony showcased ten triumphs of unbridled scholarly curiosity. In Psychology, Shigeru Watanabe, Junko Sakamoto, and Masumi Wakita of Keio University in Tokyo won for training pigeons to peck keys that discriminated between the impressionist paintings of Claude Monet and the cubist canvases of Pablo Picasso—demonstrating that birds rewarded with hemp seeds can master modern art history. In Physics, D.M.R. Georget, R. Parker, and A.C. Smith of the Institute of Food Research in Norwich, England, were honored for their rigorous mechanical analysis of soggy breakfast cereal, published in Powder Technology as 'A Study of the Effects of Water Content on the Compaction Behaviour of Breakfast Cereal Flakes.' Meanwhile, Atlanta coffee merchant John Martinez claimed the Nutrition Prize for educating the world about Luak Coffee—the world's most expensive brew, made from coffee beans ingested and excreted by the Indonesian palm civet (the luak).

Anatomical audacity and everyday bodily discomfort dominated the medical and health categories. Surgeons David B. Busch and James R. Starling of Madison, Wisconsin, captured the Literature Prize for their deeply penetrating review in the journal Surgery, 'Rectal Foreign Bodies: Case Reports and a Comprehensive Review of the World's Literature.' Their scholarly citations cataloged an unforgettable inventory of extracted items: seven light bulbs, a knife sharpener, two flashlights, a wire spring, a snuff box, an oil can with a potato stopper, eleven forms of fruits and vegetables, a jeweler's saw, a frozen pig's tail, a tin cup, a beer glass, and one patient's remarkable ensemble collection consisting of spectacles, a suitcase key, a tobacco pouch, and a magazine. In Public Health, Martha Kold Bakkevig of Sintef Unimed in Norway and Ruth Nielsen of the Technical University of Denmark won for their exhaustive study, 'Impact of Wet Underwear on Thermoregulatory Responses and Thermal Comfort in the Cold.' Medicine honored Marcia E. Buebel, David S. Shannahoff-Khalsa, and Michael R. Boyle for 'The Effects of Unilateral Forced Nostril Breathing on Cognition,' while Minnesota dentist Robert H. Beaumont took Dentistry for his incisive study, 'Patient Preference for Waxed or Unwaxed Dental Floss.'

Commercial chemistry, high-stakes finance, and parliamentary brawling closed out the 1995 celebration. Beverly Hills fashion designer Bijan Pakzad won the Chemistry Prize for creating DNA Cologne and DNA Perfume—neither of which contains a single trace of deoxyribonucleic acid, and both of which come packaged in a biologically impossible triple-helix bottle. The Economics Prize was awarded jointly to rogue trader Nick Leeson and his superiors at Barings Bank, and to Orange County, California treasurer Robert Citron, for using the calculus of financial derivatives to demonstrate that every financial institution has its limits. Finally, the Taiwan National Parliament received the Peace Prize for demonstrating that politicians gain far more by punching, kicking, and gouging each other inside the legislature than by waging war against other nations.

article_paragraphs: 1996年的第六届搞笑诺贝尔奖将科学实验的狂野与冷幽默推上了新高度。英国阿斯顿大学物理学家罗伯特·马修斯凭《翻滚的吐司、墨菲定律与基本常数》摘得物理学奖：他严密推导出，受地球引力与宇宙基本常数决定的人类身高及餐桌高度所限，吐司从桌边滑落时刚好只来得及在空中翻转半圈，因此涂黄油的那一面总是宿命般地朝下拍在地毯上！如果说马修斯揭示了餐桌上的宿命，普渡大学的乔治·戈布尔则用暴力化学重塑了后院烧烤：他把液态氧直接浇在木炭上，创下三秒钟点燃烧烤架（顺便把烤架炸飞）的世界纪录，火热捧走化学奖。挪威卑尔根大学的安德斯·巴海姆与霍格纳·桑德维克则因测试《麦芽酒、大蒜与酸奶油对水蛭食欲的影响》获颁生物学奖。

医学、公卫与生物多样性奖项则充满了荒诞剧色彩。格陵兰与挪威医生埃伦·克莱斯特和哈拉尔·莫伊发表了令人瞠目的医学报告《通过充气娃娃传播的淋病》，追踪了一起在远洋渔船船员间因共用充气娃娃而引发的离奇感染，斩获公共卫生奖；布法罗大学的罗伯特·真科医生则因发现“缺钱带来的财务压力是破坏性牙周病的高危指标”而拿到经济学奖。日本名古屋的冈村长之助更是脑洞清奇，他在石灰岩薄片里看图说话，宣称发现了长度不足百分之一英寸的微型恐龙、微型马、微型飞龙乃至“微型公主”等上千种远古微缩化石，独揽生物多样性奖；而马萨诸塞州的唐·费瑟斯通则因发明风靡全美草坪的“粉红塑料火烈鸟”荣膺艺术奖。

年度最辛辣的三记耳光分别扇向了学界、商界与政界。文化研究名刊《社会文本》的编辑们获颁文学奖，因为他们兴高采烈地发表了物理学家艾伦·索卡尔蓄意杜撰的恶搞论文《超越界限：迈向引力量子力学的变革性诠释学》——编辑们自己根本看不懂，作者事后坦言全文胡扯，文中甚至宣称“客观现实并不存在”。医学奖颁给了雷诺、菲利普·莫里斯等七大烟草公司的总裁高管，嘲讽他们在美国国会听证会上集体发誓作证的“伟大医学发现”：尼古丁绝对不会让人上瘾！和平奖则授予法国总统雅克·希拉克，表彰他在广岛原子弹爆炸五十周年之际，居然选择在太平洋引爆一连串核试验来“隆重纪念”和平。

title_en: Butter-Side-Down Toast and a Three-Second Liquid-Oxygen Barbecue
subtitle_en: The 1996 Ceremony: Cosmic Murphy's Law, Beer-Loving Leeches, Mini-Princess Fossils, and the Sokal Hoax
article_paragraphs_en: The sixth Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre in October 1996 elevated deadpan theoretical physics and explosive backyard chemistry to new heights. British physicist Robert Matthews of Aston University captured the Physics Prize for his European Journal of Physics paper, 'Tumbling Toast, Murphy's Law and the Fundamental Constants.' Matthews rigorously demonstrated that because the height of a dining table is governed by human stature—which is itself constrained by chemical bonds and the fundamental constants of the universe—a slice of toast sliding over the table's edge only has time to complete half a somersault before hitting the carpet, dooming the buttered side to land face-down! If Matthews explained breakfast tragedy, Purdue University engineer George Goble perfected backyard pyrotechnics: he won the Chemistry Prize for igniting a charcoal barbecue grill in a blistering world-record time of three seconds using liquid oxygen. Meanwhile, Norwegian researchers Anders Bærheim and Hogne Sandvik of the University of Bergen took the Biology Prize for their tasty and tasteful report in the British Medical Journal, 'Effect of Ale, Garlic, and Soured Cream on the Appetite of Leeches.'

Medical caution, dental economics, and microscopic pareidolia defined the middle slate of awards. Physicians Ellen Kleist of Nuuk, Greenland, and Harald Moi of Oslo, Norway, received the Public Health Prize for their cautionary medical case report in Genitourinary Medicine, 'Transmission of Gonorrhea Through an Inflatable Doll,' tracing a bizarre venereal infection aboard a fishing vessel. At the University at Buffalo, Dr. Robert J. Genco won the Economics Prize for his discovery that 'financial strain is a risk indicator for destructive periodontal disease'—proving that money stress can literally cost you your gums and teeth. The Biodiversity Prize honored Chonosuke Okamura of the Okamura Fossil Laboratory in Nagoya, Japan, who peered into polished limestone and claimed to discover the fossils of dinosaurs, horses, dragons, princesses, and more than 1,000 other extinct 'mini-species,' each measuring less than one-hundredth of an inch in length. In Art, Don Featherstone of Fitchburg, Massachusetts, was celebrated for his ornamentally evolutionary invention: the plastic pink flamingo.

The sharpest satirical barbs of 1996 were reserved for postmodern academia, Big Tobacco, and nuclear diplomacy. The editors of the journal Social Text won the Literature Prize for eagerly publishing physicist Alan Sokal's deliberate parody paper, 'Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity'—research that the editors could not understand, that the author said was meaningless, and which claimed that physical reality does not exist. The Medicine Prize was presented to seven tobacco executives—James Johnston of R.J. Reynolds, Joseph Taddeo of U.S. Tobacco, Andrew Tisch of Lorillard, William Campbell of Philip Morris, Edward A. Horrigan of Liggett Group, Donald S. Johnston of American Tobacco, and the late Thomas E. Sandefur Jr. of Brown & Williamson—for their unshakable discovery, as testified to the U.S. Congress, that nicotine is not addictive. Finally, French President Jacques Chirac received the Peace Prize for commemorating the fiftieth anniversary of Hiroshima with atomic bomb tests in the Pacific.

title: 电子宠物的摸鱼帝国与龙卷风拔鸡毛测速法
subtitle: 从风挡玻璃上的虫尸图鉴、圣经密码到电梯音乐防感冒，1997年的科学怪才们把脑洞开到了外太空与垃圾邮件箱。

featured_prize.winners: 伯纳德·冯内古特 (Bernard Vonnegut，纽约州立大学奥尔巴尼分校)
featured_prize.topic: 以拔鸡毛作为龙卷风风速的测量标准
featured_prize.caption: 既然风速计会被龙卷风吹碎，为什么不用一只被吹秃的母鸡来推算风速呢？大气物理学家冯内古特认真研究了“龙卷风拔鸡毛”的流体力学真相。

article_paragraphs: 1997年第七届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院首次实现全球网络直播，这一年的科学视野堪称上天入地、无所不包。天文学奖颁给了新泽西州的理查德·霍格兰，他信誓旦旦地在月球背面“发现”了十英里高的摩天大楼，还宣称火星上那块著名的岩石阴影是一张外星人雕琢的人脸。相比之下，气象学奖得主、著名作家库尔特·冯内古特的亲哥哥伯纳德·冯内古特则脚踏实地得多：他深入探究了《以拔鸡毛作为龙卷风风速的测量标准》，指出龙卷风过后活鸡之所以会全身赤裸，并非单纯被狂风硬生生拔毛，而是极度惊吓引发了家禽的心理性“羽落反应”，导致毛囊瞬间松弛脱落。

如果开车穿过风暴区，挡风玻璃上免不了啪啪作响，佛罗里达大学的马克·霍斯泰特勒便凭专著《你车上的那团黏糊物》斩获昆虫学奖，手把手教车主通过玻璃上的虫尸爆浆形状与颜色来鉴定昆虫种类。物理学奖得主、德克萨斯农工大学的约翰·博克里斯更是当代炼金术士，他在冷聚变、将贱金属点化成真金以及电化学焚烧生活垃圾三大领域同时发力。而以色列学者多伦·维茨图姆、伊利亚胡·里普斯、约阿夫·罗森伯格与美国作家迈克尔·德罗斯宁则凭吹毛求疵的统计法斩获文学奖，他们宣称用等距字母序列破译了隐藏在《圣经》里的预言密码。

在人体与心智研究上，瑞士苏黎世大学医院、日本大阪关西医科大学与捷克布拉格的柳生隆视、瓦克曼、木下、广田、河内、孔达科尔、柯尼希与莱曼跨国团队，因测量人们咀嚼不同口味口香糖时的脑电图复杂度而获生物学奖；威尔克斯大学的查内茨基、布伦南与西雅图穆扎克公司的哈里森则获医学奖，他们证明在电梯里听单调的背景音乐能刺激免疫球蛋白分泌，从而预防普通感冒。英国萨里大学的哈罗德·希尔曼凭饱含人文关怀的报告《不同死刑执行方式可能带来的痛苦》捧走和平奖。而在数字时代黎明，日本万代公司的真板亚纪与横井昭裕因发明电子宠物“拓麻歌子”，让全球打工人耗费数百万工时给虚拟小鸡铲屎而获经济学奖；费城的桑福德·华莱士则因风雨无阻地向全世界狂发电子垃圾邮件，毫无悬念地摘得通信奖。

title_en: Tamagotchi Time-Sinks & Tornado Chicken-Plucking Physics
subtitle_en: From windshield bug-splat field guides and Bible codes to cold-preventing elevator Muzak, the 1997 laureates stretched curiosity from outer space to spam folders.
article_paragraphs_en: Webcast live to the world for the very first time from Harvard’s Sanders Theatre, the 1997 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony spanned the heavens above and the highway asphalt below. The Astronomy Prize went to Richard Hoagland of New Jersey for identifying supposed artificial monuments across the solar system, including a sculpted human face on Mars and ten-mile-high skyscrapers rising from the far side of the Moon in his book 'The Monuments of Mars.' Back in Earth’s turbulent atmosphere, Meteorology laureate Bernard Vonnegut—distinguished atmospheric physicist and older brother of novelist Kurt Vonnegut—tackled a classic rural legend in his paper 'Chicken Plucking as Measure of Tornado Wind Speed.' Vonnegut demonstrated that birds found naked after a twister are not stripped purely by supersonic gale forces; rather, sheer terror triggers a physiological 'flight-molt' response that loosens their feather follicles.

For motorists driving through calmer weather, University of Florida entomologist Mark Hostetler earned the Entomology Prize for his indispensable field guide 'That Gunk on Your Car,' which teaches drivers how to identify insect species solely from the color, texture, and geometry of the bug splats smeared across their windshields. In the laboratory, Physics laureate John Bockris of Texas A&M University was honored for his audaciously wide-ranging pursuits in cold fusion, the alchemical transmutation of base elements into gold, and the electrochemical incineration of domestic garbage. Meanwhile, the Literature Prize recognized Israeli researchers Doron Witztum, Eliyahu Rips, and Yoav Rosenberg, alongside American journalist Michael Drosnin, for their hairsplitting statistical claim that equidistant letter sequences in the Book of Genesis conceal a prophetic 'Bible Code.'

Human physiology and everyday obsessions rounded out a memorable roster. An international neuroscience team—T. Yagyu, J. Wackermann, T. Kinoshita, T. Hirota, K. Kochi, I. Kondakor, Thomas König, and Dietrich Lehmann from Zurich, Osaka, and Prague—captured the Biology Prize by wiring volunteers to multichannel EEG caps to measure how different chewing gum flavors alter brainwave complexity. Medicine laureates Carl J. Charnetski and Francis X. Brennan, Jr. of Wilkes University, together with James F. Harrison of Muzak Ltd., cheered office workers everywhere by discovering that listening to soft elevator Muzak boosts secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) levels and may help ward off the common cold. On a far grimmer clinical note, Harold Hillman of the University of Surrey received the Peace Prize for his lovingly rendered study 'The Possible Pain Experienced During Execution by Different Methods.' Finally, the dawn of digital distraction claimed two prizes: Akihiro Yokoi of Wiz Company and Aki Maita of Bandai won in Economics for inventing the Tamagotchi virtual pet and diverting millions of productive work-hours into digital poultry husbandry, while self-appointed spam king Sanford Wallace of Cyber Promotions took home the Communications Prize for tirelessly blanketing the globe with electronic junk mail.

article_paragraphs: 1998年第八届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了人类挑战生理与物理极限的满腔热血与执着。安全工程奖得主、加拿大安大略省北湾的特洛伊·赫图比斯与灰熊邂逅幸存后，耗时七年倾家荡产研制出“防灰熊全身装甲”，并亲自穿上这套重型盔甲被大卡车猛撞、遭棒球棍围殴、滚下陡峭悬崖，拍成经典纪录片《灰熊计划》。同样关爱野生动物的还有葛底斯堡学院的彼得·方，他把抗抑郁药“百忧解”投喂给淡水蛤蜊，显著促进了蛤蜊排卵繁殖，凭“增进蛤蜊幸福感”斩获生物学奖。而印度总理瓦杰帕伊与巴基斯坦总理谢里夫则因在同年相继“极具侵略性又充满和平意味地”引爆原子弹，共同分享了极具讽刺意味的和平奖。

这一年还诞生了搞笑诺贝尔奖史上首位“梅开二度”的传奇得主：曾在1991年首届盛典因“水有记忆”获奖的法国学者雅克·本维尼斯特再夺化学奖，因为他进一步宣称水的顺势疗法记忆不仅真实存在，还能数字化后通过电话线和互联网跨大西洋远程传输！同样玄妙的还有物理学奖得主迪帕克·乔普拉，他将高深的量子物理学强行嫁接到生命、自由与追求经济幸福的畅销心灵鸡汤中；纽约大学荣休教授多洛雷斯·克里格则因推广“治疗性触摸”获科学教育奖——护士只要小心翼翼地避免触碰病人身体，隔空比划就能操控患者的“能量场”。芝加哥的理查德·锡德更放出豪言，企图通过克隆自己和其他人类来振兴世界经济，因而获颁经济学奖。

在直面人体尴尬的医学与心理学领域，多伦多西奈山医院的杰拉德·贝恩与阿尔伯塔大学的凯里·西米诺斯基经过严谨测量，发表《身高、阴茎长度与脚掌大小之间的关系》，用详实的统计数据击碎民间传言，荣获统计学奖。英国威尔士纽波特皇家格温特医院的米尔斯、卢埃林、凯利和霍尔特四位医生与“患者Y”共享医学奖，他们在《柳叶刀》上记录了这位男子拔鸡毛时扎破手指，导致感染罕见厌氧细菌并散发腐臭味长达五年的离奇病例。而华盛顿特区的精神分析学家玛拉·西多利博士则凭论文《放屁作为抵御难以言喻之恐惧的防御机制》摘得文学奖，证明一个适时的响屁正是幼童对抗存在主义焦虑的终极心理防御武器。

title_en: The Grizzly-Proof Iron Man & Prozac-Popping Happy Clams
subtitle_en: From transatlantic water memory over telephone lines and a five-year putrid finger to farting away existential dread, 1998 celebrated fearless human persistence.
article_paragraphs_en: The 1998 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony saluted indomitable physical courage and eccentric compassion. Leading the charge in Safety Engineering was Troy Hurtubise of North Bay, Ontario, who survived a brush with a grizzly bear and spent the next seven years building the 'Ursus' series of bear-proof body armor. As chronicled in the National Film Board of Canada documentary 'Project Grizzly,' Hurtubise personally tested his suit by having biker gangs swing baseball bats at him, throwing himself down rocky cliffs, and getting rammed repeatedly by a three-ton pickup truck. Over in the Biology category, Peter Fong of Gettysburg College brightened the lives of mollusks by dosing fingernail clams with the antidepressant Prozac; his study proved that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors trigger vigorous clam spawning at ten times the normal rate. Meanwhile, the Peace Prize delivered biting geopolitical satire, honoring Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif for their 'aggressively peaceful' tit-for-tat explosions of atomic bombs.

History was also made in Chemistry when French immunologist Jacques Benveniste—already the 1991 Ig Nobel Chemistry laureate for claiming that water retains a homeopathic 'memory' of solutes long after they are diluted away—became the first two-time Ig Nobel winner. His 1998 follow-up asserted that water’s memory can be digitized and transmitted across the Atlantic Ocean via telephone lines and the Internet to imprint fresh water thousands of miles away. In Physics, wellness guru Deepak Chopra was cited for his creative appropriation of quantum mechanics to explain life, liberty, and the pursuit of economic happiness in books like 'Quantum Healing.' Science Education went to New York University Professor Emerita Dolores Krieger for championing 'Therapeutic Touch,' a nursing technique that manipulates patients' energy fields by carefully avoiding any physical contact with them whatsoever, while Chicago physicist Richard Seed won in Economics for his enterprising plan to jump-start the global economy by cloning himself and other human beings.

Finally, researchers fearless enough to confront human awkwardness claimed the remaining honors. Jerald Bain of Mount Sinai Hospital in Toronto and Kerry Siminoski of the University of Alberta earned the Statistics Prize for their painstakingly measured clinical report 'The Relationships Among Height, Penile Length, and Foot Size,' which debunked locker-room folklore with hard regression data. The Medicine Prize was awarded jointly to 'Patient Y' and his physicians Caroline Mills, Meirion Llewelyn, David Kelly, and Peter Holt at Royal Gwent Hospital in Wales for their cautionary 'Lancet' case report 'A Man Who Pricked His Finger and Smelled Putrid for 5 Years' after puncturing his skin on a chicken bone. Rounding out the evening, Washington analytical psychologist Dr. Mara Sidoli received the Literature Prize for her illuminating psychoanalytic treatise 'Farting as a Defence Against Unspeakable Dread,' detailing how a troubled young boy used flatulence as an acoustic shield against existential terror.

article_paragraphs: 1999年第九届搞笑诺贝尔奖洋溢着浓郁的英式下午茶气息与甜点风情。物理学奖一分为二：英国与澳大利亚物理学家伦·费舍尔利用毛细管流体力学方程，精确算出了将饼干浸入热茶而不至于泡软断落杯底的最佳倾角与浸泡秒数；英比学者让-马克·范登-布鲁克与美国数学家约瑟夫·凯勒则算出了如何消除液体表面张力的附壁效应，造出倒茶绝不滴漏的茶壶嘴。与之绝配的是文学奖得主英国标准协会，他们郑重其事地发布了长达六页的国家标准规范（BS-6008），对泡一杯正宗英式茶的水温、奶量和时间做出了严苛规定。而在大洋彼岸，多伦多约克大学的史蒂夫·彭福德则因撰写关于加拿大甜甜圈店社会史的博士论文，拿下了社会学奖。

饮食与日常生活的怪诞发明同样层出不穷。新墨西哥州立大学辣椒研究所所长保罗·博斯兰博士耗时多年培育出一种完全不辣的墨西哥辣椒，让怕辣人士也能体面吃椒，荣获生物学奖；挪威斯图尔的阿尔维德·瓦特勒医生则因长年仔细收集、分类并潜心思考患者提交尿液样本时选用的五花八门容器（从果酱玻璃罐到威士忌酒瓶），摘得医学奖。为了拯救社交体面与婚姻危机，韩国首尔科隆公司的权赫镐发明了摩擦面料即可自动散发香水的商务西装，获颁环境保护奖；日本大阪安全侦探社社长牧野武则因参与研发能让妻子喷在丈夫内裤上检测出轨痕迹的“S-Check”化学喷雾，抱走了化学奖。

本年度最令人瞠目结舌的莫过于三项硬核跨界大奖。美国堪萨斯州与科罗拉多州教育委员会因规定学生“不必相信达尔文的进化论，就像不必相信牛顿的万有引力定律、法拉第与麦克斯韦的电磁学理论或巴斯德的细菌致病论一样”，被授予科学教育奖；南非约翰内斯堡的查尔·富里与米歇尔·王发明了配备检测电路与车底火焰喷射器的汽车防盗报警器，凭“把劫匪烤成焦炭”的威慑力斩获和平奖；而已故的纽约与加州发明家乔治与夏洛特·布朗斯基夫妇则因一项疯狂专利获管理医疗保健奖——他们发明了一张高速旋转的圆形分娩转盘桌，把临产孕妇绑在上面飞速旋转，试图利用强大的离心力把婴儿直接“甩”出产道！

title_en: The Fluid Dynamics of Biscuit Dunking & Centrifugal Childbirth
subtitle_en: From non-dripping teapots and infidelity-detecting underwear spray to a high-speed rotating birthing turntable, 1999 closed out the 1990s in spectacular style.
article_paragraphs_en: The 1999 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony at Harvard’s Sanders Theatre was steeped in the refined rituals of British afternoon tea and North American comfort food. The Physics Prize was shared by two breakthroughs in everyday beverage mechanics: physicist Len Fisher of the UK and Australia applied Washburn’s capillary-flow equation to calculate the exact optimal angle and duration for dunking a digestive biscuit into hot tea without suffering catastrophic soggy collapse, while Jean-Marc Vanden-Broeck and Joseph Keller calculated how to contour a teapot spout lip so that surface tension no longer makes tea dribble down the porcelain. Fittingly, the Literature Prize went to the British Standards Institution for its deadpan six-page regulatory specification (BS-6008) prescribing the official, standardized method for brewing a proper cup of tea. Across the Atlantic, York University historian Steve Penfold earned the Sociology Prize for his doctoral dissertation examining the social life, commercial history, and working-class community role of Canadian donut shops.

Culinary curiosity and everyday domestic anxieties inspired several more winners. Dr. Paul Bosland, director of the Chile Pepper Institute at New Mexico State University in Las Cruces, received the Biology Prize for breeding the 'NuMex Primavera,' a completely spiceless jalapeño pepper that delivers all the verdant aroma of a jalapeño with zero capsaicin burn. In Norway, general practitioner Dr. Arvid Vatle of Stord won the Medicine Prize for meticulously collecting, classifying, and contemplating the eclectic array of household containers—ranging from jam jars and tomato-puree tins to miniature whiskey bottles—that his patients chose when submitting urine samples. Meanwhile, Hyuk-ho Kwon of South Korea’s Kolon Company took home the Environmental Protection Prize for inventing the self-perfuming business suit embedded with scent microcapsules that release fragrance whenever the wearer rubs his sleeves, and Takeshi Makino, president of the Safety Detective Agency in Osaka, won in Chemistry for developing 'S-Check,' an over-the-counter infidelity-detection spray that wives can apply to their husbands' underwear to reveal suspicious biological traces.

The final trio of prizes showcased unforgettable extremes in education, urban security, and obstetrics. The Kansas State Board of Education and the Colorado State Board of Education shared the Science Education Prize for mandating that schoolchildren should not be required to believe in Charles Darwin’s theory of evolution any more than they believe in Isaac Newton’s theory of gravitation, Michael Faraday and James Clerk Maxwell’s theory of electromagnetism, or Louis Pasteur’s theory that germs cause disease. The Peace Prize honored Charl Fourie and Michelle Wong of Johannesburg, South Africa, for patenting the 'Blaster,' an anti-hijacking automobile burglar alarm consisting of a foot-pedal detection circuit and dual under-door liquefied-petroleum flamethrowers. Topping off the evening, the Managed Health Care Prize was awarded posthumously to George and Charlotte Blonsky of New York and San Jose for US Patent #3,216,423: an apparatus to aid women in giving birth by strapping the expectant mother onto a circular turntable and spinning it at high speed so centrifugal force gently flings the baby out.

title: 飞翔的磁悬浮青蛙与“越无知越自信”的达克效应
subtitle: 千禧年盛典诞生了科学史上的双料传奇：从未来诺奖得主的悬浮活蛙、改变心理学史的达克效应，到核磁共振仪里的爱情。

featured_prize.topic: 利用强磁场抗磁性让一只活青蛙悬浮在半空中
featured_prize.caption: 在16特斯拉的强磁场中，生物体内的水分子产生抗磁性，让一只活青蛙克服重力优雅悬浮。十年后的2010年，海姆因石墨烯再获真正的诺贝尔物理学奖，成就“双冠王”佳话！

article_paragraphs: 2000年第十届搞笑诺贝尔奖堪称科学史上的传奇里程碑，诞生了多项真正写入教科书的经典研究。心理学奖颁给了康奈尔大学的大卫·邓宁与伊利诺伊大学的贾斯汀·克鲁格，他们那篇谦逊的论文《既不称职又不自知：难以认识自身无能如何导致膨胀的自我评估》，提出了如今家喻户晓的“达克效应”。物理学奖得主、荷兰奈梅亨大学的安德烈·海姆与英国布里斯托大学的迈克尔·贝里爵士则用强磁场利用抗磁性让一只活青蛙优雅地悬浮在半空中；十年后的2010年，海姆因石墨烯研究摘得真正的诺贝尔物理学奖，成为史上唯一同时囊括搞笑诺贝尔奖与诺贝尔奖的“双冠王”！

在探究爱情与身体奥秘方面，意大利比萨大学的玛拉齐蒂、罗西、卡萨诺与加州大学圣迭戈分校的阿基斯卡尔荣获化学奖，他们发现从血小板血清素转运体等生化指标来看，浪漫热恋与患有严重强迫症几乎毫无区别。荷兰格罗宁根的舒尔茨、范安德尔、穆亚特与阿姆斯特丹的萨贝利斯则更进一步，让志愿者情侣钻进狭窄的核磁共振仪里行房，凭发表在《英国医学杂志》上的《男女交合及女性性兴奋期间生殖器的磁共振成像》斩获医学奖。相比之下，文鲜明牧师则将婚姻做成了规模经济，从1960年的36对新人一路扩张到1997年的3600万对新人集体结婚，凭“集体婚礼产业的高效增长”获颁经济学奖。

千禧年的饮食与生活同样充满荒诞色彩。澳大利亚“食气主义”教母洁丝慕音出版《靠光生活》，宣称人类其实根本不需要吃饭，靠呼吸空气和阳光就能存活，因此获文学奖；达尔豪斯大学的理查德·瓦瑟苏格则亲口生嚼热带雨林蝌蚪，凭第一手味觉测评报告《哥斯达黎加旱季几种蝌蚪的适口性比较》获生物学奖。为拯救铲屎官的文档，亚利桑那州的克里斯·尼斯万德发明了能自动识别猫咪踩键盘并拦截乱码的软件“PawSense”，摘得计算机科学奖；苏格兰格拉斯哥的怀亚特、麦克诺顿与塔利特三位医生因记录多起市民如厕时老旧瓷马桶突然碎裂坍塌伤人的惨剧，荣获公共卫生奖；而英国皇家海军则因囊中羞涩，下令水兵在实弹演习中停止发射真炮弹，改由全员齐声大喊“砰！”来代替开炮，毫无争议地赢得了和平奖。

prizes.winners: David Dunning（康奈尔大学）与 Justin Kruger（伊利诺伊大学）
prizes.summary: 发表《既不称职又不自知》，发现能力欠缺者往往高估自身水平（即著名的“达克效应”）。
prizes.winners_en: David Dunning (Cornell University) and Justin Kruger (University of Illinois)
prizes.summary_en: For their modest report 'Unskilled and Unaware of It,' establishing the Dunning-Kruger Effect.

prizes.winners: Jasmuheen（原名 Ellen Greve，澳大利亚）
prizes.summary: 出版食气主义著作《靠光生活》，宣称人类虽然吃食物，但其实完全不需要进食。
prizes.winners_en: Jasmuheen (formerly Ellen Greve, Australia)
prizes.summary_en: First lady of Breatharianism, for her book 'Living on Light,' explaining that people don't ever really need to eat food.

prizes.winners: Richard Wassersug（加拿大达尔豪斯大学）
prizes.summary: 亲口品尝并撰写第一手报告《哥斯达黎加旱季几种蝌蚪的适口性比较》。
prizes.winners_en: Richard Wassersug (Dalhousie University, Canada)
prizes.summary_en: For his first-hand taste-testing report 'On the Comparative Palatability of Some Dry-Season Tadpoles from Costa Rica.'

prizes.winners: Andre Geim（荷兰奈梅亨大学）与 Sir Michael Berry（英国布里斯托大学）
prizes.summary: 利用强磁场抗磁性让一只活青蛙悬浮在半空中（海姆于2010年再获诺贝尔物理学奖）。
prizes.winners_en: Andre Geim (University of Nijmegen) and Sir Michael Berry (Bristol University)
prizes.summary_en: For using magnets to levitate a live frog (Geim later won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics).

prizes.winners: Donatella Marazziti、Alessandra Rossi、Giovanni B. Cassano（意大利）及 Hagop S. Akiskal（美国）
prizes.summary: 发现从生物化学指标来看，浪漫热恋与患有严重强迫症（OCD）几乎无法区分。
prizes.winners_en: Donatella Marazziti, Alessandra Rossi, Giovanni B. Cassano (Italy), and Hagop S. Akiskal (USA)
prizes.summary_en: For discovering that, biochemically, romantic love may be indistinguishable from having severe obsessive-compulsive disorder.

prizes.winners: 文鲜明牧师（Reverend Sun Myung Moon）
prizes.summary: 为集体婚礼产业带来高效率与稳定增长，从36对新人婚礼一路扩张至3600万对。
prizes.winners_en: The Reverend Sun Myung Moon
prizes.summary_en: For bringing efficiency and steady growth to the mass-marriage industry, from 36 couples in 1960 to 36 million couples in 1997.

prizes.winners: Willibrord Weijmar Schultz、Pek van Andel、Eduard Mooyaart 与 Ida Sabelis（荷兰）
prizes.summary: 发表《男女交合及女性性兴奋期间生殖器的磁共振成像（MRI）》。
prizes.winners_en: Willibrord Weijmar Schultz, Pek van Andel, Eduard Mooyaart, and Ida Sabelis (The Netherlands)
prizes.summary_en: For their illuminating BMJ study 'Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Male and Female Genitals During Coitus and Female Sexual Arousal.'

prizes.winners: Chris Niswander（美国亚利桑那州图森市）
prizes.summary: 发明“PawSense”防猫踩键盘软件，能自动检测猫咪在电脑键盘上散步并锁定输入。
prizes.winners_en: Chris Niswander (Tucson, Arizona)
prizes.summary_en: For inventing PawSense, software that detects when a cat is walking across your computer keyboard.

prizes.winners: 英国皇家海军（British Royal Navy）
prizes.summary: 下令水兵在训练中停止使用昂贵的实弹炮弹，改由口头大喊“砰！（Bang!）”代替。
prizes.winners_en: The British Royal Navy
prizes.summary_en: For ordering its sailors to stop using expensive live cannon shells during training and instead just shout 'Bang!'

prizes.winners: Jonathan Wyatt、Gordon McNaughton 与 William Tullett（苏格兰格拉斯哥）
prizes.summary: 发表令人警醒的医学报告《格拉斯哥的马桶坍塌事件》。
prizes.winners_en: Jonathan Wyatt, Gordon McNaughton, and William Tullett (Glasgow, Scotland)
prizes.summary_en: For their alarming medical report 'The Collapse of Toilets in Glasgow.'

title_en: The Levitating Frog & The Birth of the Dunning-Kruger Effect
subtitle_en: The millennium ceremony produced two icons of modern science: a magnetically levitated live frog by a future Nobel laureate, and the psychology of inflated incompetence.
article_paragraphs_en: The 2000 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony—marking the tenth anniversary of the awards—stands as a landmark in scientific history, honoring two studies that became household touchstones around the world. The Psychology Prize went to David Dunning of Cornell University and Justin Kruger of the University of Illinois for their deceptively modest paper 'Unskilled and Unaware of It: How Difficulties in Recognizing One’s Own Incompetence Lead to Inflated Self-Assessments,' which introduced the world to the Dunning-Kruger Effect. Equally iconic was the Physics Prize, awarded to Andre Geim of the University of Nijmegen and Sir Michael Berry of Bristol University for using a powerful 16-Tesla electromagnet to levitate a live frog via diamagnetism. Exactly ten years later, in 2010, Geim won the Nobel Prize in Physics for isolating graphene, making him the first—and still only—person in history to win both an Ig Nobel Prize and a Nobel Prize individually.

Matters of the heart, passion, and matrimony were dissected with clinical precision. In Chemistry, Donatella Marazziti, Alessandra Rossi, and Giovanni B. Cassano of the University of Pisa, together with Hagop S. Akiskal of the University of California, San Diego, discovered that biochemically—specifically in blood platelet serotonin transporter levels—being head-over-heels in romantic love is virtually indistinguishable from suffering severe obsessive-compulsive disorder. Taking anatomical curiosity inside the scanner, Dutch researchers Willibrord Weijmar Schultz, Pek van Andel, Eduard Mooyaart, and Ida Sabelis won the Medicine Prize for their 'BMJ' paper 'Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Male and Female Genitals During Coitus and Female Sexual Arousal,' proving that volunteering couples could consummate love inside a cramped MRI tube. On a macroeconomic scale, the Reverend Sun Myung Moon received the Economics Prize for bringing steady exponential growth to the mass-marriage industry, expanding from a 36-couple wedding in 1960 to a reported 36,000,000-couple wedding in 1997.

The remaining laureates tackled quirky survival, culinary bravery, and domestic hazards. Australian 'Breatharian' guru Jasmuheen (formerly Ellen Greve) won the Literature Prize for her book 'Living on Light,' which insists that human beings never actually need to eat food if they nourish themselves on air and sunlight. In contrast, Dalhousie University biologist Richard Wassersug earned the Biology Prize for his first-hand gustatory report 'On the Comparative Palatability of Some Dry-Season Tadpoles from Costa Rica,' for which he personally chewed and graded tropical tadpoles. Computer Science honored Chris Niswander of Tucson, Arizona, for inventing 'PawSense,' software that detects when a cat is strolling across your computer keyboard and blocks feline gibberish. Public Health went to Glasgow emergency physicians Jonathan Wyatt, Gordon McNaughton, and William Tullett for their alarming report 'The Collapse of Toilets in Glasgow,' documenting injuries from crumbling Victorian porcelain commodes, while the Peace Prize saluted the British Royal Navy for ordering sailors to save money during gunnery drills by shouting 'Bang!' instead of firing live cannon shells.

title: 公元2001年重新发明轮子与浴帘内吸之谜
subtitle: 从黑洞即地狱的宇宙神学、为了省遗产税硬撑着不死，到高空坠落椰子与活性炭防臭屁内裤，21世纪初的脑洞无奇不有。

article_paragraphs: 步入21世纪的2001年第十一届搞笑诺贝尔奖，首先用一项匪夷所思的专利震惊了世界：澳大利亚维多利亚州霍桑市的律师约翰·基奥在公元2001年郑重其事地将“轮子”包装成“一种促进移动的圆形装置”申请专利，而澳大利亚专利局竟不假思索地盖章签发了第2001100012号创新专利，双方因此携手共享技术奖！同样解开日常千古之谜的还有马萨诸塞大学的大卫·施密特，他利用流体力学计算机模拟证明花洒喷水会在浴室内形成水平低压涡旋，部分解答了“为什么洗澡时浴帘总是向内飘并贴在湿漉漉的人身上”，荣获物理学奖。麦吉尔大学的彼得·巴斯则奔赴热带岛屿，凭深入调查树上掉下沉重椰子砸伤头骨的医学报告《坠落椰子导致的创伤》摘得医学奖。

人体与生老病死的荒诞规律同样逃不过学者们的法眼。科罗拉多州普韦布洛的巴克·韦默为了造福肠胃胀气的伴侣，发明了配有可更换活性炭滤芯的气密防臭屁内裤“Under-Ease”，将难闻气体扼杀在逃逸之前，荣获生物学奖；印度班加罗尔国家精神卫生与神经科学研究所的安德拉德与斯里哈里则通过详尽的问卷普查，得出了“挖鼻孔在青少年群体中是一种极其普遍的行为”这一惊人医学发现，斩获公共卫生奖。而在金钱与死亡的终极博弈中，密歇根大学商学院的乔尔·斯莱姆罗德与不列颠哥伦比亚大学的沃伊切赫·科普楚克分析遗产税申报数据后获经济学奖：他们发现如果多活几天能适用更低的遗产税率，临终富人真的会想方设法推迟死亡时间！

精神世界与文化奇观更是百花齐放。密歇根州电视布道师杰克·范·伊姆佩博士与妻子雷克塞拉在节目中惊人宣布，宇宙中的黑洞在各项技术指标上完美符合《圣经》对“地狱”位置的所有要求，双双获颁天体物理学奖；俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的劳伦斯·舍曼因观察幼儿园孩童并发表《学龄前儿童小组中幸灾乐祸与狂喜的生态学研究》获心理学奖；英国波士顿的约翰·理查兹创立“撇号保护协会”，誓死捍卫英语中复数与所有格撇号的语法尊严，摘得文学奖；立陶宛格鲁塔斯的企业家维柳马斯·马利瑙斯卡斯则因收集前苏联废弃雕像、打造名为“斯大林世界”的主题游乐园，捧走了和平奖。

prizes.summary: 发表极具“冲击力”的热带创伤医学报告《坠落椰子导致的创伤》。
prizes.winners_en: Peter Barss (McGill University, Canada)
prizes.summary_en: For his impactful medical trauma report 'Injuries Due to Falling Coconuts.'

prizes.winners: David Schmidt（美国马萨诸塞大学）
prizes.summary: 通过流体力学涡旋模拟，部分解答了“为什么淋浴时浴帘总是向内飘”的千古难题。
prizes.winners_en: David Schmidt (University of Massachusetts)
prizes.summary_en: For his computational fluid-dynamics solution to the question of why shower curtains billow inwards.

prizes.winners: Buck Weimer（美国科罗拉多州普韦布洛）
prizes.summary: 发明“Under-Ease”防屁臭气密内裤，内置可更换活性炭滤芯以过滤难闻气体。
prizes.winners_en: Buck Weimer (Pueblo, Colorado)
prizes.summary_en: For inventing Under-Ease, airtight underwear with a replaceable charcoal filter that removes bad-smelling gases before they escape.

prizes.winners: Joel Slemrod（密歇根大学）与 Wojciech Kopczuk（不列颠哥伦比亚大学）
prizes.summary: 研究发现如果推迟死亡能享受更低的遗产税率，人们会想方设法多撑几天再死。
prizes.winners_en: Joel Slemrod (University of Michigan) and Wojciech Kopczuk (University of British Columbia)
prizes.summary_en: For their conclusion that people find a way to postpone their deaths if that qualifies them for a lower rate on the inheritance tax.

prizes.winners: John Richards（英国波士顿，撇号保护协会创始人）
prizes.summary: 表彰其为保护、推广和捍卫英语中复数与所有格撇号（'）区别所做的不懈努力。
prizes.winners_en: John Richards (Boston, England, founder of The Apostrophe Protection Society)
prizes.summary_en: For his tireless efforts to protect, promote, and defend the differences between plural and possessive.

prizes.winners: Lawrence W. Sherman（美国俄亥俄州迈阿密大学）
prizes.summary: 发表研究报告《学龄前儿童小组中幸灾乐祸与狂喜（Glee）的生态学研究》。
prizes.winners_en: Lawrence W. Sherman (Miami University, Ohio)
prizes.summary_en: For his influential developmental research report 'An Ecological Study of Glee in Small Groups of Preschool Children.'

prizes.winners: Jack Van Impe 博士与 Rexella Van Impe（美国密歇根州）
prizes.summary: 在电视布道中宣布发现宇宙黑洞完全符合《圣经》中关于“地狱”位置的所有技术要求。
prizes.winners_en: Dr. Jack and Rexella Van Impe (Jack Van Impe Ministries, Michigan)
prizes.summary_en: For their discovery that cosmic black holes fulfill all the technical requirements to be the location of Hell.

prizes.winners: Viliumas Malinauskas（立陶宛格鲁塔斯）
prizes.summary: 收集前苏联时代的雕像与遗物，创建了名为“斯大林世界”的主题游乐园。
prizes.winners_en: Viliumas Malinauskas (Grutas, Lithuania)

title_en: Patenting the Wheel in 2001 & The Shower-Curtain Vortex
subtitle_en: From black holes serving as biblical Hell and postponing death to cut estate taxes to falling coconuts and charcoal-filtered underwear, 2001 was pure ingenuity.
article_paragraphs_en: Entering the twenty-first century, the 2001 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony opened with a masterclass in bureaucratic absurdity. The Technology Prize was awarded jointly to Melbourne patent lawyer John Keogh, for successfully patenting the wheel in the year 2001—described in legalese as a 'circular transportation facilitation device'—and to the Australian Patent Office for dutifully granting him Innovation Patent #2001100012 without noticing that the Mesopotamians had beaten him to it by five millennia. Solving an equally enduring domestic mystery, University of Massachusetts mechanical engineer David Schmidt won the Physics Prize for using computational fluid dynamics to explain why shower curtains billow inward toward the bather: the spray creates a horizontal low-pressure vortex much like a miniature sideways cyclone. Meanwhile, McGill University physician Peter Barss received the Medicine Prize for his impactful tropical trauma paper 'Injuries Due to Falling Coconuts,' documenting the skull-crushing kinetic energy of ripe coconuts plummeting from tall palms.

Bodily habits and the economics of mortality yielded three more unforgettable laureates. In Biology, Buck Weimer of Pueblo, Colorado, was honored for inventing 'Under-Ease,' airtight polyurethane briefs equipped with a replaceable activated-charcoal filter that traps and deodorizes flatulence before it can escape into polite company. In Public Health, Chittaranjan Andrade and B.S. Srihari of India’s National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences in Bangalore won for their probing epidemiological survey 'A Preliminary Survey of Rhinotillexomania in an Adolescent Sample,' confirming empirically that teenagers across every socioeconomic stratum pick their noses nearly four times a day. And in Economics, Joel Slemrod of the University of Michigan and Wojciech Kopczuk of the University of British Columbia analyzed estate tax returns in 'Dying to Save Taxes,' concluding that wealthy individuals somehow manage to postpone their own deaths by several days if surviving past a statutory cutoff date qualifies their heirs for a lower inheritance tax rate.

The remaining awards celebrated cosmic theology, preschool pandemonium, grammar vigilance, and post-Soviet tourism. Television evangelists Dr. Jack and Rexella Van Impe of Jack Van Impe Ministries in Rochester Hills, Michigan, earned the Astrophysics Prize for announcing on their March 2001 broadcast that cosmic black holes fulfill every single technical requirement described in Scripture to serve as the literal physical location of Hell. Miami University psychologist Lawrence W. Sherman won in Psychology for his classic observational study 'An Ecological Study of Glee in Small Groups of Preschool Children,' charting how infectious shrieks of collective joy and mischief ripple through kindergarten classrooms. In Literature, retired British journalist John Richards of Boston, England—founder of the Apostrophe Protection Society—was saluted for his heroic one-man crusade defending the grammatical distinction between plural nouns and possessive apostrophes on shopkeepers' signs, while Lithuanian mushroom entrepreneur Viliumas Malinauskas of Grutas received the Peace Prize for rounding up discarded Soviet statues to build the satirical open-air theme park known as 'Stalin World.'

title: 给印度大象算表面积与啤酒泡沫的指数衰减
subtitle: 从向饲养员求偶的英国鸵鸟、四条腿的元素周期表真桌子、肚脐眼绒毛普查，到华尔街把“虚数”写进财报，2002年妙趣横生。

featured_prize.topic: 估算印度象的总表面积
featured_prize.caption: 如何给一头动来动去的亚洲象测量全身表面积？两位印度学者耗时多年测量了24头大象的肩高与前脚周长，推导出了精确的线性回归公式：S = -8.245 + 6.807H + 7.073FFC！

featured_prize.topic_en: Estimation of the Total Surface Area in Indian Elephants

article_paragraphs: 2002年第十二届搞笑诺贝尔奖将数学与物理的严谨发挥到了极致。数学奖颁给了印度喀拉拉邦农业大学的斯里库马尔与已故的尼尔马兰，他们为了帮兽医计算给大象用药的精确剂量，拿着卷尺测量了24头亚洲象，最终推导出通过肩高与前脚周长估算《印度象总表面积》的数学公式。德国慕尼黑大学的阿恩德·莱克则把实验室搬进了啤酒馆，通过严谨记录不同种类啤酒泡沫高度随时间的变化，证明啤酒泡沫的消散完美服从数学上的“指数衰减定律”，斩获物理学奖。而横跨美瑞两国的西奥多·格雷则玩起了英文“Table”的一语双关，亲手收集多种真实化学元素样本并打造成一张长着四条腿的木制“元素周期表桌子”，抱走化学奖。

在人与动物的奇妙互动中，英国学者诺玛·布比尔、帕克斯顿、鲍尔斯与迪明荣获生物学奖，他们的论文《英国农场饲养条件下鸵鸟对人类的求偶行为》发现，养殖场里的鸵鸟见到人类饲养员走近时，竟会频频扇动翅膀、曲膝大跳求偶舞，对人的热情远胜同类。为了跨越物种障碍，日本玩具公司社长佐藤庆太、音响专家铃木松美与兽医小暮规夫联合发明了计算机狗语自动翻译机“汪语通”，因促进人狗和谐共处而获和平奖；西班牙塔拉戈纳的爱德华多·塞古拉则发明了全自动猫狗宠物洗衣机，让阿猫阿狗享受喷淋清洗、消毒除虱与水力按摩一条龙服务，摘得卫生学奖。

对人类自身的观察同样令人捧腹。悉尼大学的卡尔·克鲁泽尔尼茨基对人类肚脐眼绒毛展开了史上最全面的普查，查清了肚脐毛球的产生时间、颜色与重量，证明多毛微胖中年男性的腹毛最易把衣物纤维卷进肚脐，荣获跨学科研究奖；伦敦大学学院的克里斯·麦克马纳斯则在《自然》杂志发表《人类与古代雕塑中的阴囊不对称性》，细致考证了真人与古希腊雕塑中左右睾丸的高低与大小差异，获颁医学奖；中密苏里州立大学的吉尔与克赖纳因证实二手书上原有的乱划重点会严重干扰后人阅读理解而获文学奖。至于年度经济学奖，则一举颁给了安然、世通、安达信、施乐、美林、默克、泰科、俄罗斯天然气工业等二十八家陷入财务丑闻的跨国巨头与审计机构，讽刺他们创造性地将数学中的“虚数”概念引入了商业财务报表！

title_en: Surface Area of Indian Elephants & Exponential Beer Froth Decay
subtitle_en: From ostriches flirting with British farmers and a four-legged Periodic Table Table to Wall Street's imaginary numbers, 2002 turned everyday oddities into quantitative science.
article_paragraphs_en: The 2002 Ig Nobel Prize ceremony celebrated the triumph of mathematical rigor and literal-minded ingenuity over the messiness of the natural world. The Mathematics Prize honored K.P. Sreekumar and the late G. Nirmalan of Kerala Agricultural University in India for their painstaking report 'Estimation of the Total Surface Area in Indian Elephants,' which measured 24 Asian elephants to derive an equation predicting total pachyderm surface area from shoulder height and forefoot circumference. In Physics, Arnd Leike of the University of Munich demonstrated that a freshly poured mug of beer is a legitimate physics laboratory, proving that disappearing beer froth strictly obeys the mathematical Law of Exponential Decay. Meanwhile, American-Swiss author Theodore Gray won the Chemistry Prize for taking the phrase 'Periodic Table' literally—constructing a handsome four-legged wooden conference table containing actual physical samples of the chemical elements embedded under each square.

Interspecies romance, communication, and hygiene dominated the animal sciences. British researchers Norma Bubier, Charles G.M. Paxton, Phil Bowers, and D. Charles Deeming earned the Biology Prize for their paper 'Courtship Behaviour of Ostriches Towards Humans Under Farming Conditions in Britain,' documenting how farmed ostriches frequently flutter their wings and perform amorous mating dances for their human caretakers rather than for fellow ostriches. Bridging the communication gap with man’s best friend, Takara Co. president Keita Sato, acoustic scientist Dr. Matsumi Suzuki, and veterinarian Dr. Norio Kogure won the Peace Prize for inventing 'Bow-Lingual,' a computerized collar-and-microphone gadget that translates dog barks into human sentences. And for pets in need of a scrub, Spanish inventor Eduardo Segura of Lavakan de Aste received the Hygiene Prize for patenting a fully automated, coin-operated washing and drying machine for cats and dogs.

Turning the magnifying glass back onto human anatomy and folly yielded the final four honors. University of Sydney science broadcaster Karl Kruszelnicki won the Interdisciplinary Research Prize for his exhaustive survey of human belly button lint—establishing once and for all that slightly overweight, hairy middle-aged men wearing blue cotton shirts are the primary producers of navel fluff because abdominal hair channels fibers inward. In Medicine, Chris McManus of University College London received the prize for his balanced 1976 'Nature' report 'Scrotal Asymmetry in Man and in Ancient Sculpture,' noting that classical Greek sculptors accurately depicted the right testicle as higher than the left, yet erroneously sculpted the lower left testicle as larger. Literature honored Vicki Silvers Gier and David S. Kreiner of Central Missouri State University for proving that pre-existing, inappropriate yellow highlighter marks in used textbooks actively sabotage reading comprehension. Finally, the Economics Prize was awarded collectively to the executives, directors, and auditors of Enron, WorldCom, Arthur Andersen, Xerox, Merrill Lynch, Tyco, Gazprom, and 21 other scandal-ridden corporations for creatively adapting the mathematical concept of 'imaginary numbers' for use in corporate balance sheets.

article_paragraphs: 2003年第十三届搞笑诺贝尔奖在哈佛大学桑德斯剧院热闹揭晓，把“墨菲定律”式的幽默推向了高潮。工程学奖追授给已故的约翰·保罗·斯塔普、爱德华·墨菲以及尚在人世的乔治·尼科尔斯，表彰他们在1949年火箭雪橇试验中共同催生了那条令全人类瑟瑟发抖的铁律：“凡是可能出错的事，就一定会出错。”而在南半球的剪羊毛棚里，澳大利亚学者杰克·哈维、约翰·卡尔弗诺、沃伦·佩恩、史蒂夫·考利、迈克尔·劳伦斯、大卫·斯图尔特与罗宾·威廉姆斯对绵羊展开了严谨的力学测量，凭借《在各种表面上拖拽绵羊所需力量的分析》斩获物理学奖，证明倾斜木板配特定纹理地面拖羊最省力。

自然界与城市雕像同样充满了意外惊喜。荷兰鹿特丹自然历史博物馆的塞斯·莫利克夺得生物学奖，他在博物馆玻璃幕墙外亲眼目睹并科学记录了绿头鸭中首例有据可查的“同性恋恋尸癖”行为；瑞典斯德哥尔摩大学的斯特凡诺·吉尔兰达、莉塞洛特·扬松与马格努斯·恩奎斯特捧走跨学科研究奖，其论文《鸡更喜欢漂亮的人类》证实鸡对人类面孔颜值的审美偏好竟与大学生高度一致。日本金泽大学的广濑幸雄则因潜心化验金泽市一尊从不招惹鸽子的日本武尊青铜雕像而摘得化学奖——原来铜合金里富含剧毒的砷与铅，连鸽子都懂得趋吉避凶。

回到人类社会，伦敦大学学院的埃莉诺·马圭尔、大卫·加迪安、英格丽·约翰斯鲁德、卡特里奥娜·古德、约翰·阿什伯纳、理查德·弗拉科维亚克与克里斯托弗·弗里斯荣膺医学奖，脑部核磁共振扫描证实伦敦出租车司机的海马体比普通市民更发达。罗马大学的吉安·维托里奥·卡普拉拉、克劳迪奥·巴巴拉内利与斯坦福大学的菲利普·津巴多在心理学奖研究中指出，《政客独特而简单的性格》只需“精力”与“诚实”两个维度即可概括。纽约巴鲁克学院的约翰·特林考斯凭八十多篇统计反戴棒球帽、穿白球鞋、浅水区游来回及超市快速通道超件等日常烦心事的报告拿下文学奖；卡尔·施瓦茨勒与列支敦士登公国因推出“整国出租”服务办年会与婚礼赢得经济学奖；印度北方邦的拉尔·比哈里在被官方宣告“合法死亡”后顽强生活、发起死后维权运动并创立“死人协会”，众望所归地捧走和平奖。

title_en: Murphy's Law, Sheep-Dragging Physics, and London Cabbies' Super-Brains
subtitle_en: From the Engineering Iron Law of Catastrophe to Pigeon-Repelling Statues and the Association of Dead People
article_paragraphs_en: The 13th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony at Harvard's Sanders Theatre in 2003 elevated everyday catastrophe to high art by honoring the birth of Murphy's Law. The Engineering Prize was awarded to the late John Paul Stapp, the late Edward A. Murphy, Jr., and George Nichols, who in 1949 formulated the immortal principle during rocket-sled deceleration tests: 'If there are two or more ways to do something, and one of those ways can result in a catastrophe, someone will do it'—better known as 'If anything can go wrong, it will.' Meanwhile, down in the shearing sheds of Australia, Jack Harvey, John Culvenor, Warren Payne, Steve Cowley, Michael Lawrance, David Stuart, and Robyn Williams captured the Physics Prize for their irresistible ergonomic treatise, 'An Analysis of the Forces Required to Drag Sheep over Various Surfaces,' proving that a 1-in-10 sloped ramp with parallel wooden slats offers the least frictional resistance when hauling a stubborn fifty-kilogram ewe.

Nature and urban statues proved equally full of surprises. C.W. (Kees) Moeliker of the Natuurhistorisch Museum Rotterdam won the Biology Prize after a mallard duck crashed into his museum's glass facade and another male mallard promptly arrived to perform the first scientifically documented case of homosexual necrophilia in the species. Over at Stockholm University, Stefano Ghirlanda, Liselotte Jansson, and Magnus Enquist claimed the Interdisciplinary Research Prize for 'Chickens Prefer Beautiful Humans,' demonstrating that chickens peck preferentially at composite faces rated most attractive by university students. In Japan, Yukio Hirose of Kanazawa University took home the Chemistry Prize for investigating why a bronze statue of the mythological hero Yamato Takeru in Kanazawa never attracts pigeons—revealing that the alloy was laced with arsenic and lead, which kept the birds wisely at bay.

Back in human society, Eleanor Maguire, David Gadian, Ingrid Johnsrude, Catriona Good, John Ashburner, Richard Frackowiak, and Christopher Frith of University College London earned the Medicine Prize by showing via MRI brain scans that London taxi drivers possess significantly more developed posterior hippocampi than ordinary citizens after mastering 'The Knowledge.' Conversely, Gian Vittorio Caprara and Claudio Barbaranelli of the University of Rome, joined by Stanford's Philip Zimbardo, won the Psychology Prize for 'Politicians' Uniquely Simple Personalities,' proving voters reduce politicians' characters from the usual Big Five traits down to just two: energy and honesty. New York business professor John Trinkaus received the Literature Prize for publishing more than eighty meticulous statistical reports about things that annoyed him—from the percentage of youths wearing baseball caps backward to shoppers exceeding item limits in express checkout lanes, drivers rolling through stop signs, and students who despise Brussels sprouts. Rounding out the night, Karl Schwärzler and the nation of Liechtenstein won the Economics Prize for making it possible to rent the entire country by the night for corporate conventions, weddings, and bar mitzvahs, while Lal Bihari of Uttar Pradesh, India, won the Peace Prize for a triple triumph: leading an active life after being declared legally dead by bribed officials, waging a spirited posthumous campaign against bureaucratic inertia and greedy relatives, and founding the Association of Dead People.

article_paragraphs: 2004年第十四届搞笑诺贝尔奖将聚光灯投向了人类视觉盲区与日常生活的奇思妙想。心理学奖颁给伊利诺伊大学的丹尼尔·西蒙斯与哈佛大学的克里斯托弗·查布里斯，他们用经典的“看不见的大猩猩”实验证明：当人们全神贯注于数传球次数时，哪怕一个穿大猩猩道具服的女人大摇大摆走过球场中央，也会被半数观察者彻底忽略。在物理学奖得主、渥太华大学的拉梅什·巴拉苏布拉马尼安与康涅狄格大学及哈斯金斯实验室的迈克尔·特维眼中，转呼啦圈则是复杂的多体节生物控制论课题。佛罗里达州奥兰多的唐纳德·史密斯及其已故父亲弗兰克·史密斯，则因给掩盖秃顶的“地方支援中央”式梳头法申请美国专利而摘下工程学奖。

声音与海洋同样暗藏玄机。日本兵库县的井上大佑因发明卡拉OK荣膺和平奖，评委会盛赞他为人类提供了一种全新的“学会互相容忍”的方式；而在大洋深处，加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚大学的本·威尔逊、西蒙菲莎大学的劳伦斯·迪尔、苏格兰海洋科学协会的罗伯特·巴蒂、丹麦奥胡斯大学的马格努斯·瓦尔伯格与瑞典国家渔业局的哈坎·韦斯特伯格共同夺得生物学奖，他们发现鲱鱼在黑暗中竟是通过肛门排出气泡、“放屁”发声来互通情报的。相比之下，美国韦恩州立大学的史蒂文·斯塔克与奥本大学的詹姆斯·冈德拉赫拿下略带忧伤的医学奖，其统计报告《乡村音乐对自杀的影响》指出广播里乡村音乐播放量越大的城市，白人自杀率往往越高。

饮食、信仰与文献领域同样妙趣横生。当时就读于芝加哥农业科学高中及霍华德大学的吉莉安·克拉克凭借检验“食物掉在地上五秒内捡起来还能不能吃”的“五秒规则”赢得公共卫生奖，证实地面一旦有细菌，食物接触瞬间即被污染。英国可口可乐公司则尴尬地领走化学奖，因为他们利用所谓“尖端技术”把普通自来水包装成透明瓶装水“达萨尼”，却因检出致癌物溴酸盐超标而不得不紧急召回、禁止向消费者供应。此外，梵蒂冈因将海量弥撒祈祷业务外包给印度神父而斩获经济学奖；位于佛罗里达州基西米的美国天体主义研究图书馆则因妥善保存裸体主义历史文献、“以便每个人都能一览无余”，幽默地捧走了文学奖。

title_en: Invisible Gorillas, the Five-Second Rule, and Farting Herrings
subtitle_en: From the Karaoke Peace Prize to Patented Combovers and Outsourced Vatican Prayers
article_paragraphs_en: The 14th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2004 shone a bright light on human blind spots and ingenious everyday inventions. The Psychology Prize went to Daniel Simons of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and Christopher Chabris of Harvard University for their legendary 'Gorillas in Our Midst' experiment, which proved that when people pay close attention to counting basketball passes, roughly half fail to notice a woman in a gorilla suit strolling right through the scene and beating her chest. Movement of a more circular kind captivated Physics Prize winners Ramesh Balasubramaniam of the University of Ottawa and Michael Turvey of the University of Connecticut and Haskins Laboratory, who modeled the multisegmental biomechanics and coordination modes required to keep a hula hoop spinning. Meanwhile, Donald J. Smith and his late father, Frank J. Smith of Orlando, Florida, earned the Engineering Prize for U.S. Patent #4,022,227: the strategic three-directional 'combover' designed to conceal baldness without a wig.

Soundwaves above and below water yielded equally memorable breakthroughs. Daisuke Inoue of Hyogo, Japan, won the Peace Prize for inventing karaoke, receiving a standing ovation at Sanders Theatre for 'providing an entirely new way for people to learn to tolerate each other.' Deep beneath the waves, an international team—Ben Wilson of the University of British Columbia, Lawrence Dill of Simon Fraser University, Robert Batty of the Scottish Association for Marine Science, Magnus Wahlberg of the University of Aarhus, and Håkan Westerberg of Sweden's National Board of Fisheries—shared the Biology Prize for discovering that Pacific and Atlantic herrings communicate in the dark by squeezing gas bubbles out of their anal ducts, producing high-frequency 'Fast Repetitive Tick' (FRT) farting sounds. On a more somber acoustic note, Steven Stack of Wayne State University and James Gundlach of Auburn University received the Medicine Prize for 'The Effect of Country Music on Suicide,' showing that metropolitan areas with greater country music radio airtime experience higher white suicide rates.

Public health, corporate chemistry, and globalized faith rounded out the 2004 roster. High school apprentice Jillian Clarke of the Chicago High School for Agricultural Sciences and Howard University won the Public Health Prize for putting the folkloric 'Five-Second Rule' to the laboratory test—discovering that E. coli bacteria transfer to dropped gummy bears and cookies almost instantaneously on smooth tiles, and also noting that women are more likely than men to eat dropped food. The Chemistry Prize was bestowed upon The Coca-Cola Company of Great Britain for using 'advanced technology' to convert ordinary Thames tap water into Dasani bottled water, only to pull the entire product line from British shelves after it was found contaminated with carcinogenic bromate. Finally, the Vatican won the Economics Prize for outsourcing excess Mass prayer requests to priests in India, while the American Nudist Research Library of Kissimmee, Florida, took home the Literature Prize for 'preserving nudist history so that everyone can see it.'

article_paragraphs: 2005年第十五届搞笑诺贝尔奖见证了跨越世纪的惊人耐心与脑洞大开的奇观。物理学奖授予澳大利亚昆士兰大学的约翰·梅恩斯通与已故的托马斯·帕内尔，表彰他们自1927年起苦苦守候的“沥青滴漏实验”——漏斗中凝固的黑色沥青平均每九年才缓慢滴落一滴。同样考验耐力的还有营养学奖得主、日本东京发明家中松义郎博士，他连续三十四年为自己吃下的每一顿饭拍照并进行回顾性分析。而在新西兰梅西大学，詹姆斯·沃森凭借学术论文《理查德·巴克利先生爆炸的裤子之重要意义》摘得农业史奖，生动还原了二十世纪三十年代新西兰奶农用氯酸钠除草剂喷洒杂草后，药液沾染裤子干燥遇火猛烈爆炸的历史。

流体与气味的研究更是令人捧腹。德国不来梅国际大学及芬兰奥卢大学的维克托·本诺·迈耶-罗乔与匈牙利罗兰大学的约瑟夫·加尔荣膺流体力学奖，他们运用基础物理学公式严谨计算了企鹅排便时体内积聚的惊人压强，发表了《企鹅排便时产生的压力——鸟类排便计算》。明尼苏达大学的爱德华·卡斯勒与威斯康星大学的布莱恩·格特尔芬格则往泳池里倒入瓜尔胶，通过实验解答“人在糖浆里游泳比在水里更快还是更慢”而拿下化学奖，证实二者速度几乎难分伯仲。生物学奖颁给本杰明·史密斯、克雷格·威廉姆斯、迈克尔·泰勒、布莱恩·威廉姆斯与早坂洋司，他们不辞辛劳地逐一嗅闻并分类记录了131种蛙类在感到压力时分泌的奇特气味。

动物福利、昆虫观影与现代科技也各显神通。密苏里州的格雷格·米勒因发明具有三种尺寸和三种软硬度的绝育公狗人造替代睾丸“Neuticles”赢得医学奖；英国纽卡斯尔大学的克莱尔·林德与彼得·西蒙斯在蝗虫观看电影《星球大战》精彩片段时，用电极监测其脑细胞活动，奇妙地捧走和平奖。麻省理工学院的高里·南达发明了会反复逃跑并躲藏起来的闹钟，因理论上能迫使人们准时下床、增加每日有效工作时长而斩获经济学奖；尼日利亚的“互联网创业者们”则因通过电子邮件向全球群发短篇故事，塑造阿巴查将军、阿巴查夫人与姆贝基大律师等急需一小笔手续费以解锁巨额财富的富豪角色，一举夺得文学奖。

title_en: Penguin Poo Pressure, the 78-Year Pitch Drop, and Swimming in Syrup
subtitle_en: From Runaway Alarm Clocks to Exploding New Zealand Trousers and Star Wars-Watching Locusts
article_paragraphs_en: The 15th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2005 celebrated monumental scientific patience alongside explosive historical curiosities. The Physics Prize went to John Mainstone and the late Thomas Parnell of the University of Queensland, Australia, who had patiently tended the famous Pitch Drop Experiment since 1927, watching a congealed glob of black tar ooze through a glass funnel at the glacial rate of roughly one drop every nine years. A rival feat of multi-decade dedication earned Dr. Yoshiro Nakamats of Tokyo the Nutrition Prize for photographing and retrospectively analyzing every single meal he had consumed over a period of thirty-four years (and counting). Meanwhile, James Watson of Massey University, New Zealand, captured the Agricultural History Prize for his scholarly paper 'The Significance of Mr. Richard Buckley's Exploding Trousers,' recounting how interwar New Zealand dairy farmers spraying ragwort weeds with sodium chlorate herbicide inadvertently turned their cotton pants into violently combustible garments.

Fluid mechanics and olfactory endurance took center stage in the middle rounds. Victor Benno Meyer-Rochow of International University Bremen and the University of Oulu, together with Jozsef Gal of Loránd Eötvös University in Hungary, won the Fluid Dynamics Prize for 'Pressures Produced When Penguins Pooh—Calculations on Avian Defaecation,' computing that penguins build up between 10 and 60 kilopascals of rectal pressure to fling guano forty centimeters clear of their nests. Over in Minnesota, chemical engineers Edward Cussler and Brian Gettelfinger thickened a twenty-five-meter swimming pool with guar gum to win the Chemistry Prize, settling a classic debate by proving that humans swim at virtually the same speed in syrup as they do in water. And an intrepid team led by Benjamin Smith, Craig Williams, Michael Tyler, Brian Williams, and Yoji Hayasaka earned the Biology Prize for painstakingly smelling and cataloging the stressed-out skin secretions of 131 different species of frogs—ranging from nutty and floral to rotten fish.

Canine dignity, cinephile insects, and digital storytelling rounded out the 2005 honors. Gregg A. Miller of Oak Grove, Missouri, received the Medicine Prize for inventing Neuticles—prosthetic replacement testicles for neutered dogs, offered in three sizes and three degrees of firmness so pets can retain their self-esteem. Newcastle University neurobiologists Claire Rind and Peter Simmons won the Peace Prize for wiring up a locust's brain to monitor its Descending Contralateral Movement Detector neuron while the insect watched action highlights from the movie 'Star Wars.' MIT graduate student Gauri Nanda claimed the Economics Prize for inventing Clocky, a wheeled alarm clock that leaps off the nightstand and hides repeatedly, forcing sleepers out of bed and theoretically adding productive hours to the global workday. Finally, the Literature Prize honored the 'Internet entrepreneurs of Nigeria' for using e-mail to distribute a bold series of short stories introducing millions of readers to a cast of wealthy characters—General Sani Abacha, Mrs. Mariam Sanni Abacha, Barrister Jon A. Mbeki Esq., and others—each requiring just a small advance fee to unlock and share a vast fortune.

article_paragraphs: 2006年第十六届搞笑诺贝尔奖在日常声光与生物奥秘中寻找笑点。鸟类学奖颁给加州大学戴维斯分校的伊万·施瓦布与加州大学洛杉矶分校已故的菲利普·梅，他们深入解释了啄木鸟每天狂啄树干上万次却不会得头痛或脑震荡的颅骨防震机制。科威特大学的瓦斯米亚·胡提与科威特环境公共管理局的法滕·穆萨拉姆斩获营养学奖，证明屎壳郎其实是不折不扣的挑食美食家；荷兰瓦赫宁根农业大学等的巴特·克诺尔斯与鲁尔德·德容则夺得生物学奖，他们发现传播疟疾的雌性冈比亚按蚊对林堡干酪气味和人类脚臭味的喜爱程度竟然旗鼓相当，毫无二致。

物理、化学与数学家们在餐桌和相机前大显身手。巴黎第六大学的巴西勒·奥多利与塞巴斯蒂安·诺伊基希荣获物理学奖，他们揭示了弯曲干意大利面条时，首次断裂瞬间释放的弹性波为何总让面条碎成三截或更多截，而非整齐的两截。西班牙瓦伦西亚大学的安东尼奥·穆莱特、何塞·哈维尔·贝内迪托、何塞·邦与巴利阿里群岛大学的卡门·罗塞略凭《温度对切达干酪中超声波传播速度的影响》拿下化学奖。澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织的尼克·斯文森与皮尔斯·巴恩斯则斩获数学奖，精确推算出拍集体照时必须连拍多少张照片，才能几乎保证现场没有任何人闭眼。

感官刺激与语言医学同样令人拍案叫绝。林恩·哈尔彭、伦道夫·布莱克与詹姆斯·希伦布兰德因实验探究人类为何极度讨厌指甲刮黑板的声音而赢得声学奖；威尔士的霍华德·斯塔普尔顿发明了发出高频刺耳噪音驱赶青少年而成年人听不见的装置，后来又用同一技术制成学生听得见但老师听不见的手机隐形铃声，奇妙地捧走和平奖。普林斯顿大学的丹尼尔·奥本海默凭论文《无论必要与否均使用博学语汇之后果：不必要地使用长词的问题》摘得文学奖，证明故意堆砌生僻大词反而会让人显得更蠢；美国田纳西大学医学院的弗朗西斯·费斯迈尔与以色列海法本·锡安医疗中心的马吉德·奥德、哈里·巴桑、阿里·奥利文则因先后发表同名医学病例报告《用手指直肠按摩终止顽固性打嗝》，共同分享了医学奖。

title_en: Shattering Spaghetti, Shock-Proof Woodpeckers, and Cheese-Loving Mosquitoes
subtitle_en: From Fingernails on a Blackboard and Teenager Repellents to Blink-Free Group Photos
article_paragraphs_en: The 16th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize Ceremony in 2006 found high comedy in everyday acoustics, kitchen physics, and picky creatures. The Ornithology Prize went to Ivan R. Schwab of the University of California, Davis, and the late Philip R.A. May of UCLA for explaining why woodpeckers can hammer tree trunks twelve thousand times a day at decelerations of 1,000 g without getting headaches or concussions—thanks to spongy cranial bones, tightly packed brains, and millisecond-timed third eyelids. Culinary discernment in the insect world earned two prizes: Wasmia Al-Houty of Kuwait University and Faten Al-Mussalam of the Kuwait Environment Public Authority won the Nutrition Prize for proving that Scarabaeus cristatus dung beetles are finicky eaters that strongly prefer horse and sheep dung over camel or fox droppings, while Bart Knols and Ruurd de Jong of Wageningen Agricultural University won the Biology Prize for demonstrating that the female malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae is attracted equally to the odor of Limburger cheese and the smell of unwashed human feet.

Physicists, chemists, and mathematicians tackled puzzles of the dinner table and the family camera. Basile Audoly and Sebastien Neukirch of the Université Pierre et Marie Curie in Paris won the Physics Prize for solving a mystery that had baffled Nobel laureate Richard Feynman: why bending dry spaghetti almost always snaps it into three or more pieces rather than two (the initial break unleashes elastic flexural waves that spike curvature along the remaining rod). In Spain, Antonio Mulet, José Javier Benedito, José Bon, and Carmen Rosselló claimed the Chemistry Prize for 'Ultrasonic Velocity in Cheddar Cheese as Affected by Temperature,' showing ultrasound travels fastest through cheddar between 0 and 17 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, Nic Svenson and Piers Barnes of Australia's CSIRO won the Mathematics Prize for deriving a rule-of-thumb formula calculating how many photos you must snap of a group of N people to almost guarantee that nobody has their eyes closed.

Acoustic torment, pretentious prose, and emergency medicine delivered the evening's final laughs. D. Lynn Halpern, Randolph Blake, and James Hillenbrand won the Acoustics Prize for investigating why the sound of fingernails scraping on a blackboard sends chills down the human spine, pinpointing mid-range frequencies between 2,000 and 4,000 hertz rather than the highest pitches. Welsh inventor Howard Stapleton received the Peace Prize for creating the 'Mosquito' electromechanical teenager repellent—which emits a high-frequency buzz audible to loitering youths but inaudible to adults over thirty—and then reverse-engineering the technology into 'secret' schoolroom cellphone ringtones that students can hear while their teachers remain oblivious. Princeton psychologist Daniel Oppenheimer won the Literature Prize for 'Consequences of Erudite Vernacular Utilized Irrespective of Necessity: Problems with Using Long Words Needlessly,' proving that pompous vocabulary makes authors sound less intelligent. Finally, Francis M. Fesmire of the University of Tennessee and the Israeli team of Majed Odeh, Harry Bassan, and Arie Oliven of Bnai Zion Medical Center shared the Medicine Prize for their identically titled clinical case reports: 'Termination of Intractable Hiccups with Digital Rectal Massage.'
